```tsx
  <Card.Description>$19 / month</Card.Description>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>{/* features list */}</Card.Content>
<Card.Footer>
  <Button color="primary" block pill={false}>Choose Pro</Button>
</Card.Footer>
</Card>
```

## Checkbox
Checkbox for binary on/off selection with solid, pill, and ghost variants, an indeterminate state, and rich labels with inline descriptions.
Import: import { Checkbox } from "@plexui/ui/components/Checkbox"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/checkbox
Props:
  - variant ("solid" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Visual style: solid (filled background) or ghost (checkmark only)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded indicator corners
  - checked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Controlled state
  - defaultChecked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Initial state (uncontrolled)
  - onCheckedChange ((next: boolean) => void) — Called when state changes
  - label (ReactNode) — Accessible label. Accepts ReactNode for rich content
  - description (ReactNode) — Second line below the label, linked via aria-describedby. Renders only with a label
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction
  - required (boolean) — Required for form submission
  - name (string) — Form field name
  - value (string) — Value when submitted
  - orientation ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Label position relative to checkbox
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to wrapper node
  - id (string) — The id of the checkbox element

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
<Checkbox label="Same as billing address" />
<Checkbox label="Subscribe to newsletter" defaultChecked />
</div>
```

### With Radio Group
Place Checkbox alongside RadioGroup controls to verify that indicator sizes, label baselines, and spacing align consistently in both horizontal and vertical layouts.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full max-w-md">
<Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
  {() => (
    <RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Notification channel">
      <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      ...
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field label="Topics" description="Select the topics you want to follow.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox defaultChecked label={...} />
      ...
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Descriptions
Combine Field-level label and description with item-level descriptions for options that need additional context. Use a plain label without descriptions when the options are self-explanatory.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Email notifications" description="Configure which emails you receive.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span className="font-medium">Marketing</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Receive emails about new products and features.</span>
            </div>
          }
          defaultChecked
        />
        ...
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Push notifications">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <Checkbox label="Everything" />
        <Checkbox label="Direct messages and mentions" defaultChecked />
        <Checkbox label="Nothing" />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Variants
The checkbox supports three visual styles: solid (default) with a filled background and standard radius, solid pill with fully rounded corners, and ghost which renders only the checkmark without a border or background fill.
```tsx
{/* solid (default) */}
<Checkbox label="Checked" defaultChecked />

{/* solid pill */}
<Checkbox label="Checked" pill defaultChecked />

{/* ghost */}
<Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" defaultChecked />
```

### Pill
Set pill to render the checkbox indicator with fully rounded corners (border-radius: full) instead of the default square radius.
```tsx
<Checkbox label="Checked" pill defaultChecked />
```

### Ghost
Use variant="ghost" to render the checkbox without a border or background. The checkmark uses the text color instead of white, making it suitable for subtle inline selections or task lists.
```tsx
<Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" defaultChecked />
```

### With description
Use description for a second line under the label. It sits outside the label, so the checkbox keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby. The description renders only next to a label.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Checkbox
  label="Accept terms and conditions"
  description="By checking this box, you agree to our Terms of Service and Privacy Policy."
  defaultChecked
/>
<Checkbox
  label="Enable notifications"
  description="You can enable or disable notifications at any time from settings."
/>
</div>
```

### Indeterminate
Use checked="indeterminate" to indicate a partially selected state. This is typically used for "select all" controls where only some child items are checked.
```tsx
const [checked, setChecked] = useState<boolean | "indeterminate">("indeterminate");

<Checkbox
checked={checked}
onCheckedChange={() =>
  setChecked(c => c === "indeterminate" ? true : c ? false : "indeterminate")
}
label="Select all"
/>
```

### Disabled
When disabled is set, the checkbox is dimmed to 50% opacity and prevents interaction. Works consistently across all variants: solid, pill, and ghost.
```tsx
{/* solid */}
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" disabled />
<Checkbox label="Checked" disabled defaultChecked />
<Checkbox label="Indeterminate" disabled checked="indeterminate" />

{/* solid pill */}
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" pill disabled />
<Checkbox label="Checked" pill disabled defaultChecked />

{/* ghost */}
<Checkbox label="Unchecked" variant="ghost" disabled />
<Checkbox label="Checked" variant="ghost" disabled defaultChecked />
```

### Label orientation
By default the checkbox renders to the left of the label. Set orientation="right" to place the checkbox after the label.
```tsx
<Checkbox label="Accept terms and conditions" orientation="right" />
```

### Without label
When no label is provided, the checkbox renders as a standalone control, so pass aria-label to give it an accessible name. All three visual states are shown: unchecked, checked, and indeterminate.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-4">
<Checkbox aria-label="Accept terms" />
<Checkbox aria-label="Subscribe" defaultChecked />
<Checkbox aria-label="Select all" checked="indeterminate" />
</div>
```

### Group with select all
Combine a parent checkbox with child checkboxes to create a "select all" pattern. The parent shows an indeterminate state when only some children are checked.
```tsx
const [items, setItems] = useState([
{ id: "read", label: "Read", checked: true },
{ id: "write", label: "Write", checked: false },
{ id: "execute", label: "Execute", checked: false },
]);

const allChecked = items.every(i => i.checked);
const noneChecked = items.every(i => !i.checked);
const parentChecked = allChecked ? true : noneChecked ? false : "indeterminate";

<>
<Checkbox
  label="Permissions"
  checked={parentChecked}
  onCheckedChange={() => {
    const next = !allChecked;
    setItems(prev => prev.map(i => ({ ...i, checked: next })));
  }}
/>
<div className="pl-6 flex flex-col gap-3">
  {items.map(item => (
    <Checkbox
      key={item.id}
      label={item.label}
      checked={item.checked}
      onCheckedChange={next => {
        setItems(prev =>
          prev.map(i => i.id === item.id ? { ...i, checked: Boolean(next) } : i)
        );
      }}
    />
  ))}
</div>
</>
```

### Group with description
Wrap a group of checkboxes in a Field for a shared label and description. This is a common pattern for preference lists and settings panels.
```tsx
<Field label="Show on desktop" description="Select the items you want to display on the desktop.">
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
    <Checkbox label="Hard disks" defaultChecked />
    <Checkbox label="External disks" />
    <Checkbox label="CDs, DVDs, and iPods" />
    <Checkbox label="Connected servers" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>
```

### With Field
Wrap checkboxes in a Field component for form layout with label, description, and error message support. The Field provides aria-describedby and aria-invalid linking automatically.
```tsx
<Field
label="Terms"
description="Please review and accept the terms before continuing."
errorMessage={showError ? "You must accept the terms to continue." : undefined}
>
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
    <Checkbox label="I agree to the Terms of Service" />
    <Checkbox label="Subscribe to product updates" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate checkbox groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
<div className="divide-y">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Email notifications" description="Configure which emails you receive.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span>Marketing</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">
                Receive emails about new products and features.
              </span>
            </div>
          }
          defaultChecked
        />
        <Checkbox
          label={
            <div className="flex flex-col">
              <span>Security</span>
              <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">
                Receive emails about account activity and security.
              </span>
            </div>
          }
          defaultChecked
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Push notifications" description="Configure which push notifications you receive.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3">
        <Checkbox label="Everything" />
        <Checkbox label="Direct messages and mentions" defaultChecked />
        <Checkbox label="Nothing" />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

## Code Block
Code block with syntax highlighting, a copy button, and collapsible long snippets with configurable expanded height limits.
Import: import { CodeBlock } from "@plexui/ui/components/CodeBlock"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/code-block
Props:
  - children (string) — Code content
  - language (string) — Prism language name
  - className (string) — Additional wrapper class
  CollapsibleCodeBlock:
    - children (string) — Code content
    - language (string) — Prism language name
    - defaultExpanded (boolean) default: false — Start expanded
    - collapsedHeight (number) default: 140 — Height when collapsed (px)
    - maxExpandedHeight (number) — Max height when expanded (px)
    - copyable (boolean) default: true — Show copy button

### Overview
```tsx
<CodeBlock language="javascript">{codeSnippet}</CodeBlock>
```

### Collapsible
Use CollapsibleCodeBlock to display code in a compact view with gradient overlay and an expand action.
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx">{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Expanded by default
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx" defaultExpanded>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Custom collapsed height
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx" collapsedHeight={60}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Max expanded height
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx" defaultExpanded maxExpandedHeight={200}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Without copy button
```tsx
<CollapsibleCodeBlock language="tsx" defaultExpanded copyable={false}>{code}</CollapsibleCodeBlock>
```

### Supported languages
A pragmatic set of Prism grammars are pre-registered out of the box.
```tsx
<CodeBlock language="javascript">{code}</CodeBlock>
```

## Copy Tooltip
A copy-to-clipboard tooltip that wraps any trigger element and confirms when the value has been copied.
Import: import { CopyTooltip } from "@plexui/ui/components/Tooltip"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/copy-tooltip
Props:
  - children (ReactNode) — Trigger element (for example Tooltip.TriggerDecorator)
  - copyValue (string) — Required. Content to copy to clipboard
  - openDelay (number) default: 150 — Tooltip open delay in milliseconds
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Preferred tooltip alignment against the trigger
  - alignOffset (number) default: 0 — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "top" — Preferred side of the trigger
  - sideOffset (number) default: 5 — Distance from trigger in pixels
  - onCopy ((copied: boolean) => void) — Called once the clipboard write settles, with whether it succeeded. The tooltip says Copied! only after a successful write

### Overview
```tsx
<CopyTooltip copyValue="Very cool content to copy">
<Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>sess_12345abcdefg</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
</CopyTooltip>
```

## Date Input
Masked text input for typing dates and times, with automatic formatting, min and max limits, and validation.
Import: import { DateInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/DateInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-input
Props:
  - value (DateTime | null) — Selected date (Luxon DateTime)
  - onChange ((date: DateTime | null) => void) — Called when a complete valid date is entered or the field is cleared
  - mode (MaskitoDateMode) default: "dd/mm/yyyy" — Date format mode: dd/mm/yyyy, mm/dd/yyyy, yyyy/mm/dd, etc.
  - separator (string) default: "." — Character between date parts
  - timeMode (MaskitoTimeMode) — Enable time input: HH:MM, HH:MM:SS, etc.
  - dateTimeSeparator (string) default: ", " — Separator between date and time parts
  - timeStep (number) default: 0 — Arrow-key increment step for time (ms)
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest allowed date
  - max (DateTime) — Latest allowed date
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button when input has a value
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Input size (3xs to 3xl)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable input
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - placeholder (string) — Auto-generated from format if not set

### Overview
```tsx
const [date, setDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null)
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
```

### With time
Pass timeMode="HH:MM" to enable date + time input in one field.
```tsx
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} timeMode="HH:MM" clearable />
```

### With seconds
Use timeMode="HH:MM:SS" for second-level precision.
```tsx
<DateInput timeMode="HH:MM:SS" ... />
```

### Limits
Use min and max to restrict the date range. The mask prevents entering values outside the allowed range.
```tsx
<DateInput
min={today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf('day')}
max={today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf('day')}
clearable
/>
```

### US format
Set mode="mm/dd/yyyy" and separator="/" for US-style date formatting.
```tsx
<DateInput mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" ... />
```

### ISO format
Set mode="yyyy/mm/dd" and separator="-" for ISO 8601 formatting.
```tsx
<DateInput mode="yyyy/mm/dd" separator="-" ... />
```

### With Field
Wrap with Field to add a label, description, and automatic accessibility attributes.
```tsx
<Field label="Date of birth" description="Enter your date of birth">
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
```

### Validation
Pass errorMessage to Field to display a validation error.
```tsx
<Field label="Date of birth" errorMessage={!date ? 'Date is required' : undefined}>
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} clearable />
</Field>
```

### Disabled
```tsx
<DateInput disabled value={DateTime.local(2025, 1, 1)} onChange={...} />
```

## Date Picker
Date picker with an interactive calendar, time picker, year and month dropdowns, min/max limits, and date-of-birth presets.
Import: import { DatePicker } from "@plexui/ui/components/DatePicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-picker
Props:
  - value (DateTime | null) — Selected date (luxon)
  - onChange ((date: DateTime | null) => void) — Called when date changes
  - min (DateTime) — Minimum selectable date
  - max (DateTime) — Maximum selectable date
  - captionLayout ("buttons" | "dropdown") default: "buttons" — Calendar header mode. Use dropdown for date of birth
  - showTime (boolean) default: false — Show time input below calendar
  - yearRange ([number, number]) — Min/max years for dropdown caption
  - size (ControlSize) — Trigger size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) — Rounded trigger
  - clearable (boolean) — Show clear button
  - triggerShowIcon (boolean) default: true — Show calendar icon
  - triggerDateFormat (string) default: "MM/dd/yy" — Date format in trigger. Auto-includes time when showTime is enabled
  - placeholder (string) — Trigger placeholder
  - disabled (boolean) — Disable picker

### Overview
```tsx
const [selectedDate, setSelectedDate] = useState<DateTime | null>(null)
<DatePicker value={selectedDate} onChange={setSelectedDate} clearable pill />
```

### Limits
Use min and max to limit selectable dates to a specific timeframe.
```tsx
const minDate = today.minus({ days: 30 }).startOf('day')
const maxDate = today.plus({ days: 30 }).endOf('day')
<DatePicker value={...} onChange={...} min={minDate} max={maxDate} />
```

### Date of birth
Set captionLayout="dropdown" to add month and year dropdowns inline with the arrow navigation. Ideal for selecting a date of birth where navigating month-by-month would be impractical.
```tsx
<DatePicker
captionLayout="dropdown"
triggerDateFormat="MMMM d, yyyy"
max={DateTime.local()}
placeholder="Select your birthday"
clearable pill
/>
```

### Time picker
Enable showTime to add hour and minute inputs below the calendar. The popover stays open after selecting a date so the user can adjust the time. Use arrow keys to increment or decrement values.
```tsx
<DatePicker
showTime
triggerDateFormat="MM/dd/yy HH:mm"
placeholder="Select date & time"
clearable pill
/>
```

### Dropdown + time
Combine captionLayout="dropdown" with showTime for quick month/year jumps and time selection in a single picker, useful for scheduling events at a specific date and time.
```tsx
<DatePicker
captionLayout="dropdown"
showTime
yearRange={[2020, 2030]}
triggerDateFormat="MMM d, yyyy HH:mm"
placeholder="Schedule event"
clearable pill
/>
```

### Two fields
Compose DatePicker and Input type="time" side by side for maximum flexibility in form layouts. Each field operates independently while sharing the same DateTime value.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '12px' }}>
<div>
  <label>Date</label>
  <DatePicker value={...} onChange={...} />
</div>
<div>
  <label>Time</label>
  <Input type="time" value={...} onChange={...} />
</div>
</div>
```

### Date input
For typing a date directly instead of picking it, use DateInput, a masked input that auto-formats as you type.
```tsx
<DateInput value={date} onChange={setDate} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" />
```

### DateTime input
Pass timeMode="HH:MM" to DateInput to type the date and time in one field.
```tsx
<DateInput value={dateTime} onChange={setDateTime} mode="mm/dd/yyyy" separator="/" timeMode="HH:MM" />
```

### Without Icon
Remove the calendar icon from the trigger by setting triggerShowIcon to false.
```tsx
<DatePicker triggerShowIcon={false} placeholder="Choose a date" ... />
```

### Disabled
Disable the picker to prevent user interaction.
```tsx
<DatePicker disabled value={...} onChange={...} />
```

## Date Range Picker
Date range picker with an interactive calendar, min/max limits, preset shortcuts, and a month stepper for selecting start and end dates.
Import: import { DateRangePicker } from "@plexui/ui/components/DateRangePicker"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/date-range-picker
Props:
  - value (DateRange | null) — Selected range ([start, end], inclusive)
  - onChange ((next: DateRange | null, shortcut?: DateRangeShortcut) => void) — Called when range changes
  - min (DateTime) — Earliest selectable date
  - max (DateTime) — Latest selectable date
  - maxRangeDays (number) — Max length of range in days (inclusive)
  - shortcuts (DateRangeShortcut[]) — Quick selection shortcuts
  - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") default: "bottom" — Preferred side for popover
  - sideOffset (number) default: 8 — Distance from trigger in pixels
  - align ("start" | "center" | "end") default: "center" — Preferred popover alignment
  - alignOffset (number) default: align === "center" ? 0 : -5 — Offset from start/end alignment in pixels
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable picker interactions
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select date range..." — Placeholder in trigger when value is empty
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger style variant
  - pill (boolean) default: true — Rounded trigger shape
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Trigger size scale
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") default: "dropdown" — Icon shown at trigger end
  - triggerClassName (string) — Custom class for trigger
  - triggerShowIcon (boolean) default: true — Show calendar icon at trigger start
  - triggerStepperUnit ("month") — Enable month stepper mode in trigger
  - triggerDateFormat (string) default: "MM/dd/yy" — Date formatting in trigger text
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button in trigger
  - block (boolean) default: false — Stretch trigger to full available width

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState<DateRange | null>(null)
<DateRangePicker value={value} onChange={setValue} shortcuts={shortcuts} clearable pill />
```

### Limits
Use min and max to limit the selectable range. Use maxRangeDays to limit the range length.
```tsx
<DateRangePicker value={...} onChange={...} min={minDate} max={maxDate} />
```

### Shortcuts
Use the shortcuts array to provide quick date range options. When a shortcut is selected, its label is shown in the trigger.
```tsx
<DateRangePicker shortcuts={dayShortcuts} ... />
```

### Month stepper
Enable a stepper in the trigger with triggerStepperUnit="month". When the selected range matches the unit, the trigger shows the stepper.
```tsx
<DateRangePicker
triggerStepperUnit="month"
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
clearable
pill
max={maxDate}
/>
```

## Dialog
Modal dialog for confirmations, forms, and destructive alerts, with a focus trap, escape handling, and an overlay scrim.
Import: import { Dialog } from "@plexui/ui/components/Dialog"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/dialog
Props:
  - open (boolean) — Controlled open state
  - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when the dialog opens or closes
  Dialog.Content:
    - width (number | string) default: 480 — Panel width
    - showClose (boolean) default: true — Show close button in top-right corner
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class on the panel
    - placement ("center" | "top" | "bottom" | "start" | "end" | "fullscreen") default: "center" — Where the panel sits: centered, near the top, a bottom sheet, a side panel, or the whole screen
    - mobilePlacement ("center" | "bottom" | "fullscreen") — Placement at 640px and below; defaults to placement
    - onOpenAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called when focus moves into the dialog on open; call event.preventDefault() to place it yourself, for example on the panel instead of the first field
    - onCloseAutoFocus ((event: Event) => void) — Called when focus returns on close; call event.preventDefault() to keep it elsewhere

### Overview
```tsx
<Dialog>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="outline">Open dialog</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>Unsaved changes</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <p>You have unsaved changes that will be lost...</p>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close><Button color="primary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button></Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="primary">Save changes</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Destructive confirmation
Use color="danger" on the action button for destructive operations.
```tsx
<Dialog>
<Dialog.Trigger>
  <Button color="danger" variant="outline">Delete</Button>
</Dialog.Trigger>
<Dialog.Content>
  <Dialog.Header>
    <Dialog.Title>Delete assistant?</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Header>
  <p>This change will affect all API integrations. It cannot be undone.</p>
  <Dialog.Footer>
    <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Cancel</Button></Dialog.Close>
    <Button color="danger">Delete</Button>
  </Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

### Scrolling body
Put long content in Dialog.Body: only the body scrolls, while the header and footer stay in view. Without it the whole panel scrolls.
```tsx
<Dialog.Content>
<Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Title>Terms of service</Dialog.Title>
  <Dialog.Description>Please read them before you continue.</Dialog.Description>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>
  {terms.map((term) => <p key={term}>{term}</p>)}
</Dialog.Body>
<Dialog.Footer>
  <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Decline</Button></Dialog.Close>
  <Button color="primary">Accept</Button>
</Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
```

### Placement
Use placement to move the panel: top for search and command lists, bottom for a sheet along the bottom edge, start and end for a full-height side panel, fullscreen for the whole screen. mobilePlacement applies at 640px and below, so a centered dialog can become a bottom sheet on phones: {''}.
```tsx
<Dialog.Content placement="end" width={360}>
<Dialog.Header>
  <Dialog.Title>Filters</Dialog.Title>
</Dialog.Header>
<Dialog.Body>{/* fields */}</Dialog.Body>
<Dialog.Footer>
  <Dialog.Close><Button color="secondary" variant="soft">Clear filters</Button></Dialog.Close>
  <Button color="primary">Done</Button>
</Dialog.Footer>
</Dialog.Content>
```

## Empty Message
Empty state for telling users there's nothing to show, with error, warning, no-results, and onboarding compositions.
Import: import { EmptyMessage } from "@plexui/ui/components/EmptyMessage"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/empty-message
Props:
  - fill ("static" | "absolute" | "none") default: "static" — How the container fills its parent: "static" takes full width and height, "absolute" covers a positioned parent (inset 0), "none" applies no sizing
  - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — sm is the compact message for a panel, a card section or an empty list
  - align ("center" | "start") default: "center" — start left-aligns the message, for an empty state under a section heading
  EmptyMessage.Icon:
    - color ("secondary" | "danger" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
    - size ("sm" | "md") default: "md" — Icon size
  EmptyMessage.Title:
    - color ("secondary" | "danger" | "warning") default: "secondary" — Semantic color
  EmptyMessage.ActionRow:
    - className (string) — Additional classes for the action row container

### Composition
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon><Explore /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title>No projects yet</EmptyMessage.Title>
<EmptyMessage.Description>Create your first project to get started</EmptyMessage.Description>
<EmptyMessage.ActionRow><Button color="primary"><Plus /> New project</Button></EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Error message
The color property enables you to display clearer intent with the message, such as showing an error state.
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon color="danger"><Mic /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title color="danger">Enable microphone access...</EmptyMessage.Title>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Warning message
```tsx
<EmptyMessage>
<EmptyMessage.Icon color="warning"><Sparkle /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Title>o1-preview is in beta</EmptyMessage.Title>
<EmptyMessage.Description>System instructions and model configuration are not available yet.</EmptyMessage.Description>
<EmptyMessage.ActionRow className="text-sm">
  <TextLink href="/">Learn more<ArrowUpRight /></TextLink>
</EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### No results
The components of EmptyMessage are both composable and optional. This example omits the EmptyMessage.Title component, using only an icon and description for a simpler message style.
```tsx
<EmptyMessage fill="none">
<EmptyMessage.Icon size="sm"><Search /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
<EmptyMessage.Description>No icons found matching "pizza"</EmptyMessage.Description>
</EmptyMessage>
```

### Compact
Use size="sm" for an empty panel, card section or list: a smaller title, tighter spacing and no minimum width. Pair it with fill="none" when the container sets the height.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Members</Card.Title>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <EmptyMessage size="sm" fill="none">
    <EmptyMessage.Icon size="sm"><Group /></EmptyMessage.Icon>
    <EmptyMessage.Title>No members yet</EmptyMessage.Title>
    <EmptyMessage.Description>Invite people to work on this project.</EmptyMessage.Description>
    <EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
      <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" size="sm">Invite</Button>
    </EmptyMessage.ActionRow>
  </EmptyMessage>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

### Left aligned
Use align="start" for an empty state that sits under a section heading instead of filling a surface: a single line such as "No tags added" reads with the heading above it.
```tsx
<Card>
<Card.Header>
  <Card.Title>Tags</Card.Title>
</Card.Header>
<Card.Content>
  <EmptyMessage size="sm" align="start" fill="none">
    <EmptyMessage.Description>No tags added.</EmptyMessage.Description>
  </EmptyMessage>
</Card.Content>
</Card>
```

## Field
Form field wrapper with a label, helper text, an error message, and automatic accessibility linking to its control.
Import: import { Field } from "@plexui/ui/components/Field"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/field
Props:
  - label (ReactNode) — Label text for the field
  - description (ReactNode) — Helper text below the label; linked via aria-describedby
  - errorMessage (ReactNode) — Error message below the control; auto-sets aria-invalid on child
  - labelAction (ReactNode) — Content at the end of the label row, such as a link that acts on the field
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: child's size, else "md" — Label font size; defaults to the child control's size
  - required (boolean) default: false — Shows a required asterisk after the label (visual only)
  - orientation ("vertical" | "horizontal") default: "vertical" — Layout direction of label and control
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Applies optical alignment to the child control via negative margin using its gutter
  - id (string) — Override the auto-generated id used for htmlFor/aria linking
  - children (ReactElement | (fieldProps) => ReactNode) — Form control; receives id, aria-describedby and aria-invalid, plus aria-labelledby unless it has its own name. A render prop receives aria-labelledby to spread

### Overview
Field wraps a form control with a label, optional description, and error message. It automatically generates htmlFor, aria-describedby, and aria-invalid linking between the label, description, error, and child control.
```tsx
<Field label="Email">
<Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
```

### With description
Use description to display helper text below the label. The description is automatically linked to the control via aria-describedby.
```tsx
<Field label="Email" description="We'll never share your email with anyone else.">
<Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
```

### With error message
Use errorMessage to display a validation error. When provided, the child control automatically receives aria-invalid="true". The error is rendered using the FieldError component with role="alert" for accessibility.
```tsx
<Field label="Email" errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address">
<Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
```

### Required
Use required to show a visual asterisk after the label. This is purely visual and does not add the required HTML attribute. Pass required directly to the child control for form validation.
```tsx
<Field label="Email" required>
<Input placeholder="Enter email..." />
</Field>
```

### Sizing
The label and description scale with the child control: Field reads the control's size, so {''} gets a lg label without repeating it. Pass size to Field to set the label size yourself, or when the child is a render prop.
```tsx
<Field label="Email">
<Input placeholder="Enter email..." size="lg" />
</Field>
```

### Horizontal layout
Use orientation="horizontal" to render the label beside the control instead of above it.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Field label="First name" orientation="horizontal">
  <Input placeholder="Jane" />
</Field>
<Field label="Last name" orientation="horizontal">
  <Input placeholder="Doe" />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Textarea
```tsx
<Field label="Bio" description="Write a short bio for your profile.">
<Textarea placeholder="Tell us about yourself..." rows={3} />
</Field>
```

### Select
A Select trigger is not a native form control, so the label's htmlFor cannot name it. Field points the trigger's aria-labelledby at the label, and Select adds its value: a screen reader hears "Role, Admin". DatePicker works the same way. A control with its own aria-label, aria-labelledby or label keeps its name.
```tsx
<Field label="Role" description="Select your primary role.">
<Select
  placeholder="Select a role..."
  value={role}
  onChange={(option) => setRole(option.value)}
  options={[
    { label: "Admin", value: "admin" },
    { label: "Editor", value: "editor" },
    { label: "Viewer", value: "viewer" },
  ]}
/>
</Field>
```

### Label action
Use labelAction for a link or a small control that acts on the field, at the end of the label row: a password reset, a template switch, a "Replace" link. It takes the label's font size.
```tsx
<Field
label="Password"
labelAction={<TextLink href="/reset-password">Forgot password?</TextLink>}
>
<Input type="password" placeholder="Enter password..." />
</Field>
```

### Slider
Field works with any form control. Use the description to display the current slider value.
```tsx
const [price, setPrice] = useState([200, 800])
<Field label="Price Range" description={`Set your budget range ($${price[0]} – $${price[1]}).`}>
<Slider range value={price} onChange={setPrice} min={0} max={1000} step={10} prefixUnit="$" />
</Field>
```

### Fieldset
Group related fields under a heading and description to create a logical fieldset.
```tsx
<div>
<div className="mb-3">
  <h3 className="text-xs font-medium text-secondary uppercase tracking-wider">Address Information</h3>
  <p className="text-sm text-secondary mt-1">We need your address to deliver your order.</p>
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
  <Field label="Street Address">
    <Input placeholder="123 Main St" />
  </Field>
  <div className="flex gap-3">
    <Field label="City" className="flex-1">
      <Input placeholder="New York" />
    </Field>
    <Field label="Postal Code" className="flex-1">
      <Input placeholder="90502" />
    </Field>
  </div>
</div>
</div>
```

### Checkbox
Wrap a group of checkboxes in a Field for a shared label and description.
```tsx
<Field label="Notifications" description="Choose which notifications you'd like to receive.">
{() => (
  <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
    <Checkbox label="Email notifications" />
    <Checkbox label="Push notifications" />
    <Checkbox label="SMS notifications" />
  </div>
)}
</Field>
```

### Radio
Use Field with RadioGroup for labeled radio selections.
```tsx
<Field label="Subscription plan" description="Select your preferred plan.">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <RadioGroup aria-label="Subscription plan" value={plan} onChange={setPlan} direction="col">
    <RadioGroup.Item value="free">Free</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="pro">Pro — $9/mo</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="enterprise">Enterprise — $29/mo</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>
```

### Switch
Pair a Field with a Switch using orientation="horizontal" for inline toggle settings.
```tsx
<Field label="Marketing emails" orientation="horizontal">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <Switch id={fieldProps.id} checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />
)}
</Field>
```

### Field group
Stack Field components with a divider to group related notification settings.
```tsx
<div className="divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-6">
  <Field label="Responses" description="Get notified when the assistant responds to requests that take time.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
        <Checkbox label="Push notifications" defaultChecked />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="py-6">
  <Field label="Tasks" description="Get notified when tasks you've created have updates.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 mt-1">
        <Checkbox label="Push notifications" />
        <Checkbox label="Email notifications" />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Validation and Errors
Combine required and errorMessage for client-side validation feedback. Toggle errors on and off to see the visual transition.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Field label="Name" required errorMessage={nameError}>
  <Input placeholder="Enter your name" value={name} onChange={(evt) => setName(evt.target.value)} />
</Field>
<Field label="Email" required errorMessage={emailError}>
  <Input placeholder="Enter your email" value={email} onChange={(evt) => setEmail(evt.target.value)} />
</Field>
</div>
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign="start" to apply a negative margin on the child control, aligning its text with the surrounding content. Works with pill inputs. The label, description, and error message stay at the container edge while the control extends past it.
```tsx
<div className="border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md py-6 px-8">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-5">
  <Field label="Full name" opticallyAlign="start">
    <Input placeholder="Jane Doe" pill />
  </Field>
  <Field label="Email" description="We'll never share your email." errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address." required opticallyAlign="start">
    <Input placeholder="jane@example.com" pill />
  </Field>
</div>
<Button className="mt-6" color="primary" variant="soft" pill>Submit</Button>
</div>
```

## File Upload
Mobile-first file upload with MIME-type and size validation, multi-file selection, error states, and read-only file cards.
Import: import { FileUpload, FileCard, FileCardGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/FileUpload"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/file-upload
Props:
  - variant ("compact" | "area") default: "compact" — Visual variant: compact button or larger tappable area
  - label (string) — Button label text
  - description (string) — Helper text below the icon (area variant only)
  - accept (string) — Accepted file types (e.g. ".pdf,.png,image/*")
  - multiple (boolean) default: false — Allow selecting multiple files
  - maxFiles (number) — Maximum number of files. Button disables at limit.
  - maxSize (number) — Maximum file size in bytes
  - value (File[]) — Controlled file list
  - onValueChange ((files: File[]) => void) — Callback when files are added or removed
  - onFileReject ((file: File, reason: string) => void) — Callback when a file is rejected (wrong type, too large, over limit)
  - errorMessage (string) — Error message. Sets the invalid visual state
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid state (auto-set when errorMessage is provided)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all interactions
  FileCard:
    - file (File) — The file to display
    - onRemove (() => void) — Remove callback. When omitted, the delete button is hidden.
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the remove button
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class
  FileCardGroup:
    - children (ReactNode) — FileCard elements
    - className (string) — Additional CSS class

### Overview
```tsx
<FileUpload
accept=".pdf,.png,.jpg,.jpeg"
multiple
maxFiles={5}
maxSize={10 * 1024 * 1024}
value={files}
onValueChange={setFiles}
/>
```

### With files
File list renders below the button in a bordered pill container. Each file shows a type icon, name with middle truncation, size, and a remove button.
```tsx
const files = [
new File([], "government-id-scan.pdf"),
new File([], "passport-photo.png"),
new File([], "non-citizen-travel-2026-approved-document.pdf"),
];

<FileUpload
accept=".pdf,.png"
multiple
maxFiles={5}
value={files}
onValueChange={setFiles}
/>
```

### Error state
```tsx
<FileUpload
accept=".pdf"
multiple
value={files}
onValueChange={setFiles}
errorMessage="Please upload at least 2 documents."
/>
```

### Disabled
```tsx
<FileUpload disabled />
```

### Read-only
```tsx
<FileCardGroup>
<FileCard file={file} />
</FileCardGroup>
```

### With remove
```tsx
<FileCardGroup>
<FileCard file={file} onRemove={() => removeFile()} />
</FileCardGroup>
```

### Multiple files
```tsx
<FileCardGroup>
{files.map((file, i) => (
  <FileCard key={file.name} file={file} onRemove={() => removeFile(i)} />
))}
</FileCardGroup>
```

### Read-only list
```tsx
<FileCardGroup>
{files.map((file) => (
  <FileCard key={file.name} file={file} />
))}
</FileCardGroup>
```

## Float Input
Text input whose label floats above the value, with error and helper text, a clear button, a password reveal toggle, and a multi-line variant.
Import: import { FloatingLabelInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/floating-label-input
Props:
  - label (string) — Floating label text
  - description (ReactNode) — Helper text below the input
  - errorMessage (string) — Validation message below input; sets invalid state
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable input interactions
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid visual state
  - readOnly (boolean) default: false — Read-only input state
  - onClear (() => void) — Shows a clear button when input has value
  - startAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered before the input, inside the field. Visible when focused or has value.
  - endAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered after the input, before the clear button
  - multiline (boolean) default: false — Render as an auto-growing textarea
  - rows (number) default: 2 — Initial visible text lines when multiline is true

### Overview
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" />
```

### Filled state
When the input has a value, the label stays floated above the input.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" />
```

### Textarea
Use multiline to render an auto-growing textarea with the same floating-label treatment. The textarea starts at 2 rows and grows automatically as content is added. The border radius adjusts to half the input height.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Message" multiline />
```

### With error message
Use the errorMessage prop to display a validation error below the input. When errorMessage is provided, the input automatically enters the invalid state.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
defaultValue="jane.doe@example"
invalid
errorMessage="Email is not valid."
/>
```

### With description
Use the description prop to display helper text below the input.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
/>
```

### With description and error
When both description and errorMessage are provided, the error appears first (closest to the input), followed by the description.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
defaultValue="jane.doe@example"
invalid
errorMessage="Email is not valid."
description="We'll never share your email with anyone else."
/>
```

### Clear button
Use the onClear prop to display a built-in clear button. The button appears when the input has a value and is not disabled or read-only.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("clearable@example.com")

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Email address"
value={value}
onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
onClear={() => setValue("")}
/>
```

### Disabled
Use the disabled prop to disable the input, greying it out and preventing user interactions.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" disabled />
```

### Read only
Use the readOnly prop to make the input read-only. The user can still select and copy the text.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@example.com" readOnly />
```

### All states
Overview of all input states.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-8 py-8">
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Empty</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Filled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@gmail.com" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Invalid</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput invalid label="Email address" defaultValue="invalid@email" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Disabled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput disabled label="Email address" defaultValue="jane.doe@gmail.com" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Read only</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput readOnly label="Email address" defaultValue="readonly@gmail.com" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Password input
A type="password" field ships a built-in reveal toggle: click the eye to show or hide the value. Set revealable to false to remove it.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput label="Password" type="password" />
```

### SSN input
A Social Security Number input combining three techniques: an input mask that auto-inserts dashes (XXX-XX-XXXX) with highlighted segment, value masking that hides digits behind bullets (•••-••-••••), and a built-in revealable toggle to reveal the real value.
```tsx
const [rawDigits, setRawDigits] = useState("")
const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false)
const formatted = formatSSN(rawDigits)

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Social Security Number"
value={formatted}
inputMode="numeric"
maxLength={11}
onChange={(evt) => setRawDigits(extractDigits(evt.target.value))}
style={!visible && rawDigits ? { color: 'transparent', caretColor: 'var(--color-text)' } : undefined}
revealable
onRevealedChange={setVisible}
/>
```

### Birthday input
A date-of-birth input with inline formatting that inserts separators as you type (MM / DD / YYYY).
```tsx
const [birthday, setBirthday] = useState("")

<FloatingLabelInput
label="Birthday"
value={birthday}
maxLength={14}
onChange={(evt) => setBirthday(formatBirthdayValue(evt.target.value))}
/>
```

### Birthday with validation
Use invalid and errorMessage to display the OpenAI-style birthday validation state.
```tsx
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Birthday"
defaultValue="02 / 30 / 2001"
invalid
errorMessage="Please enter a valid date."
/>
```

### Birthday states
Overview of birthday input states.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-8 py-8">
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Empty</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Birthday" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Filled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput label="Birthday" defaultValue="01 / 15 / 1995" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Invalid</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput invalid label="Birthday" defaultValue="02 / 30 / 2001" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
<div className="flex items-center">
  <div className="text-right text-secondary text-sm mr-8 min-w-[5rem]">Disabled</div>
  <FloatingLabelInput disabled label="Birthday" defaultValue="01 / 15 / 1995" className="w-[320px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Select
Use FloatingLabelSelect for plain text dropdowns. The label floats up when a value is selected, matching FloatingLabelInput styling.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"

const [role, setRole] = useState(null)
const selected = ROLES.find((r) => r.value === role)

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Role"
    selected={!!selected}
    onClearClick={() => setRole(null)}
  >
    {selected?.label}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content>
  <Menu.RadioGroup value={role} onChange={setRole}>
    {ROLES.map((r) => (
      <Menu.RadioItem key={r.value} value={r.value}>
        {r.label}
      </Menu.RadioItem>
    ))}
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Multiple selection
Pair FloatingLabelSelect with a multiple Select to collect several values while keeping the floating-label treatment. The trigger shows the selected count and exposes a clear button that resets the whole list.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"

const [skills, setSkills] = useState([])
const hasSelection = skills.length > 0
const display = skills.length === 1
? SKILLS.find((s) => s.value === skills[0])?.label
: skills.length > 1 ? `${skills.length} skills` : ""

<Select
multiple
clearable
value={skills}
options={SKILLS}
onChange={(options) => setSkills(options.map((o) => o.value))}
block
trigger={({ open }) => (
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Skills"
    selected={hasSelection}
    open={open}
    onClearClick={hasSelection ? () => setSkills([]) : undefined}
  >
    {display}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
)}
/>
```

### Country select
Use FloatingLabelSelect alongside FloatingLabelInput for consistent form styling. The select trigger shares the same floating-label visual shell: the label floats up when a value is selected.
```tsx
import { FloatingLabelSelect } from "@plexui/ui/components/FloatingLabelSelect"
import { Menu } from "@plexui/ui/components/Menu"

const [country, setCountry] = useState(null)
const selected = COUNTRIES.find((c) => c.value === country)

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <FloatingLabelSelect
    label="Country"
    selected={!!selected}
    onClearClick={() => setCountry(null)}
  >
    {selected?.flag} {selected?.label}
  </FloatingLabelSelect>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content>
  <Menu.RadioGroup value={country} onChange={setCountry}>
    {COUNTRIES.map((c) => (
      <Menu.RadioItem key={c.value} value={c.value}>
        {c.flag} {c.label}
      </Menu.RadioItem>
    ))}
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Phone input
A country code selector paired with a FloatingLabelInput that uses startAdornment to show the dial code as a non-editable prefix. The prefix appears when the field is focused or has a value.
```tsx
<Select trigger={countryTrigger} ... />
<FloatingLabelInput
label="Phone number"
type="tel"
startAdornment={<span className="text-tertiary">+34</span>}
/>
```

## Indicators
Loading and progress indicators, from circular spinners and determinate progress rings to animated dots, with configurable color and stroke.
Import: import { LoadingIndicator, CircularProgress, LoadingDots } from "@plexui/ui/components/Indicator"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/indicators
  LoadingIndicator:
    - size (number | string) — Size in px or any CSS length (or use --indicator-size CSS variable)
    - strokeWidth (number) — Stroke width
  CircularProgress:
    - progress (number) — Static progress 0-100 (disables animation)
    - size (number | string) — Diameter in px or any CSS length
    - strokeWidth (number) — Stroke thickness
    - done (boolean) — Completion state for animation
    - trackColor (string) — Track color (CSS variable or value)
    - trackActiveColor (string) — Active segment color

### Overview
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-6">
<LoadingIndicator size={20} />
<CircularProgress size={24} />
<LoadingDots />
</div>
```

### LoadingIndicator
Simple spinning indicator for general loading states.
```tsx
<LoadingIndicator />
```

### Sizing & stroke
By default, the indicator adapts to the surrounding font-size and color of text. You can control the size of the LoadingIndicator using the --indicator-size CSS custom property.
```tsx
<LoadingIndicator size={30} strokeWidth={2} />
```

### Color
The indicator defaults to currentcolor, inheriting the surrounding text color. This can also be customized by altering the --indicator-color variable around the DOM scope of the component.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-danger">
<LoadingIndicator size={16} /> <span>Destroying forever...</span>
</div>
```

### Duration
You can control the rotation speed of the spinner with --indicator-rotate-duration.
```tsx
<div style={{ '--indicator-rotate-duration': '3s' } as React.CSSProperties}>
<LoadingIndicator />
</div>
```

### CircularProgress
Circular progress ring with simulated progress animation.
```tsx
<CircularProgress />
```

### Progress
Use progress to show static progress and prevent the animation.
```tsx
<CircularProgress progress={25} />
```

### Sizing & stroke
Use size and strokeWidth. Or use --circular-progress-size and --circular-progress-stroke CSS variables.
```tsx
<CircularProgress size={30} strokeWidth={2} />
```

### Color
Customize the color of the indicator with the --circular-progress-track-color and --circular-progress-track-active-color variables.
```tsx
<CircularProgress trackColor="var(--alpha-15)" trackActiveColor="var(--gray-1000)" />
```

### LoadingDots
Indicate typing progress with staggered pulsing dot animation.
```tsx
<LoadingDots />
```

### Color
The indicator defaults to currentcolor, inheriting the surrounding text color. You can customize the color by providing a different color value or context.
```tsx
<div className="text-danger">
<LoadingDots />
</div>
```

## Input Group
Input or textarea with icons, text, buttons and menus attached inside one frame, inline or as header and footer rows, in every input size and style.
Import: import { InputGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/InputGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/input-group
Props:
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Control height, on the same scale as Input (22px to 48px)
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the frame
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded frame, with pill buttons inside
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disables the control and the buttons inside
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid border; sets aria-invalid on the control
  - className (string) — Applied to the root <div>
  InputGroup.Addon:
    - align ("inline-start" | "inline-end" | "block-start" | "block-end") default: "inline-start" — Before or after the control on its line, or a row above or below it
    - className (string) — Applied to the addon <div>

### Overview
Put an InputGroup.Input and one or more InputGroup.Addons inside an InputGroup. The group draws the frame and passes size, pill, disabled and invalid down to the control and the buttons.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search..." />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <Search />
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>12 results</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the group, like Input.
```tsx
<InputGroup variant="outline">...</InputGroup>
<InputGroup variant="soft">...</InputGroup>
```

### Sizes
Every Input size from 3xs to 3xl. Icons, text and InputGroup.Button scale with the group: buttons in inline addons fit the control height and keep a 4px inset.
```tsx
<InputGroup size="lg">
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search..." />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <Search />
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Button>Search</InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Align
Use align on InputGroup.Addon to place it before (inline-start, the default) or after (inline-end) the control, or as a row above (block-start) or below (block-end) it. Place addons after the control in the markup so the tab order starts with the field; align handles the visual position.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Ada Lovelace" />
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-start">
  <InputGroup.Text>Full name</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Text
Use InputGroup.Text for prefixes, suffixes, units and counters. Clicking text or icons in an addon focuses the field.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="0.00" inputMode="decimal" />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <InputGroup.Text>$</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>USD</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Button
InputGroup.Button is a Button that defaults to ghost and secondary and takes its size from the group. Pass uniform for icon buttons.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input placeholder="Search the docs..." />
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Button variant="soft">Search</InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Dropdown
Wrap an InputGroup.Button in a Menu to pick a unit of measurement next to the value.
```tsx
const UNITS = [
{ value: "kg", label: "Kilograms" },
{ value: "lb", label: "Pounds" },
{ value: "st", label: "Stones" },
]
const [unit, setUnit] = useState("kg")

<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input defaultValue="72" inputMode="decimal" aria-label="Weight" />
<InputGroup.Addon>
  <InputGroup.Text>Weight</InputGroup.Text>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <Menu>
    <Menu.Trigger>
      <InputGroup.Button aria-label="Weight unit">
        {unit}
        <ChevronDownMd />
      </InputGroup.Button>
    </Menu.Trigger>
    <Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={160}>
      {UNITS.map((item) => (
        <Menu.CheckboxItem
          key={item.value}
          checked={unit === item.value}
          onCheckedChange={() => setUnit(item.value)}
          indicatorVariant="ghost"
        >
          {item.label} ({item.value})
        </Menu.CheckboxItem>
      ))}
    </Menu.Content>
  </Menu>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Spinner
Show a LoadingIndicator in an addon while a value is searched or saved.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Input defaultValue="Saving changes" readOnly />
<InputGroup.Addon align="inline-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>Saving...</InputGroup.Text>
  <LoadingIndicator />
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

### Textarea
With InputGroup.Textarea, use block-start and block-end addons for a header and a footer. Utility classes such as ml-auto push a button to the far side.
```tsx
<InputGroup>
<InputGroup.Textarea placeholder="console.log('Hello, world!');" rows={4} className="font-mono" />
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-start">
  <InputGroup.Text>
    <FileCode />
    script.js
  </InputGroup.Text>
  <InputGroup.Button uniform aria-label="Copy" className="ml-auto">
    <Copy />
  </InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
<InputGroup.Addon align="block-end">
  <InputGroup.Text>Line 1, Column 1</InputGroup.Text>
  <InputGroup.Button variant="solid" color="primary" className="ml-auto">
    Run
    <Play />
  </InputGroup.Button>
</InputGroup.Addon>
</InputGroup>
```

## Input
Text input with start and end adornments, a clear button, a password visibility toggle, and presets for SSN and birthday.
Import: import { Input } from "@plexui/ui/components/Input"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/input
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "soft" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual style of the input; ghost has no border and no fill
  - size ("3xs" | "2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl" | "2xl" | "3xl") default: "md" — Controls the size of the input
  - gutterSize ("2xs" | "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl") — Controls gutter on the edges; defaults to value from size
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disables the input visually and from interactions
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark the input as invalid
  - allowAutofillExtensions (boolean) default: type === "password" || !!name — Allow autofill extensions to appear in the input
  - autoSelect (boolean) default: false — Select all contents of the input when mounted
  - startAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the start of the input
  - endAdornment (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the end of the input
  - onClear (() => void) — When provided, displays a clear button that appears when the input has a value
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Fully rounded pill shape
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Applies a negative margin using the current gutter to optically align with surrounding content

### Overview
```tsx
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." />
```

### Variants
Use variant to stylize the input. ghost has no border and no fill, for a field its container already frames, such as the search line at the top of a dialog; it still turns red when invalid.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[320px]">
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." variant="outline" />
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." variant="soft" />
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." variant="ghost" />
</div>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the input is controlled with size and gutterSize props. size sets the input to a specific control height, and gutterSize sets the horizontal padding. Each size provides default values for gutterSize, as well as font-size. Each of these values can be overridden independently.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5 justify-start items-start w-[320px]">
<Input placeholder="Enter text..." size="lg" />
<Input placeholder="Search..." startAdornment={<Search className="fill-tertiary" />} size="lg" />
<Input value={username} placeholder="Username" onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)} maxLength={16} endAdornment={<span className="mt-[1.5px] tabular-nums text-tertiary text-[.875em]">{username.length}/16</span>} />
</div>
```

### Start adornment
You can add arbitrary content to the beginning of an input with startAdornment, like a search icon. Ideally, the spacing will look pretty good by default. If you need to customize the spacing: gutterSize determines the amount of spacing on the edges of the container, which you can fine-tune as needed (if you need precise spacing not supported by gutterSize, use negative left margin on your adornment directly, e.g. -ml-2). The spacing between the adornment and the input is controlled with gap on the container, which you can customize as needed with Tailwind classes.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Start adornment"
startAdornment={<Search className="fill-tertiary" />}
/>
```

### Clear button
Use the onClear prop to display a built-in clear button. The button appears when the input has a value and is not disabled or read-only.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Enter text..."
value={value}
onChange={(evt) => setValue(evt.target.value)}
onClear={() => setValue("")}
pill
/>
```

### End adornment
You can add arbitrary content to the end of an input with endAdornment, like a character counter or custom icon. The same spacing guidance from startAdornment applies here.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Username"
value={username}
onChange={(evt) => setUsername(evt.target.value)}
maxLength={16}
endAdornment={
  <span className="mt-[1.5px] tabular-nums text-tertiary text-[.875em]">
    {username.length}/16
  </span>
}
/>
```

### Password with visibility toggle
Combine endAdornment with an Input.AdornmentButton to switch between type="password" and type="text". Works across all sizes, variants, and with pill.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Password"
type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}
endAdornment={
  <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
    {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
  </Input.AdornmentButton>
}
/>
```

### SSN input
A masked SSN field that formats input as XXX-XX-XXXX, hides digits behind bullets when masked, and reveals the value via an Input.AdornmentButton in endAdornment. An inline mask suffix highlights the next expected segment. Adapts to all sizes automatically.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Social Security Number"
value={formatted}
inputMode="numeric"
endAdornment={
  <Input.AdornmentButton aria-pressed={visible} onClick={toggle}>
    {visible ? <EyeOff /> : <Eye />}
  </Input.AdornmentButton>
}
style={!visible && rawDigits ? { color: 'transparent', caretColor: 'var(--color-text)' } : undefined}
/>
```

### Birthday input
A date-of-birth input with inline formatting that inserts separators as you type (MM / DD / YYYY). An inline mask suffix highlights the next expected segment. Works across all sizes, variants, and with pill.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Birthday (MM / DD / YYYY)"
value={birthday}
inputMode="numeric"
maxLength={14}
/>
```

### Birthday with validation
Use invalid and FieldError to display a validation state when the entered date is not valid.
```tsx
<Input
placeholder="Birthday (MM / DD / YYYY)"
value={birthday}
inputMode="numeric"
invalid={!!errorMessage}
/>
```

### Disabled
Use the disabled prop to disable the input, greying it out and preventing user interactions.
```tsx
<Input disabled defaultValue="Jane Doe" />
```

### Invalid
Use the invalid prop to mark the input as invalid. You decide how this state is removed, whether that's through onFocus, onChange, an onSubmit handler, etc. Default visual styles will be applied, based on the variant. Additionally, [data-invalid] is applied to the container for custom styling.
```tsx
<Input invalid placeholder="Invalid input" />
```

### Auto select text
Pass autoSelect to select all text in the input, useful when pairing with other copy actions. This prop behaves like an imperative action when toggled and allows selection to change.
```tsx
<Input autoSelect placeholder="Add text..." defaultValue="Toggle to auto select" />
```

### Autofill extensions
By default, autofill extensions are prevented by Input. For the occasions where you want browser extensions to be present, pass allowAutofillExtensions to remove the disabling. When name is passed, or type is set to "password", this value will default to true.
```tsx
<Input allowAutofillExtensions name="email" placeholder="Allowed" />
```

### With button
You can pair Input and Button components together by using the same size value.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-2">
<Input placeholder="jane.doe@gmail.com" size="lg" variant="outline" />
<Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="outline" pill={false}>Subscribe</Button>
</div>
```

### Optical alignment
```tsx
<Field label="Full name" opticallyAlign="start">
<Input placeholder="Jane Doe" pill />
</Field>
<Field
label="Email"
description="We'll never share your email."
errorMessage="Please enter a valid email address."
required
opticallyAlign="start"
>
<Input placeholder="jane@example.com" pill />
</Field>
<Button className="mt-6" color="primary" variant="soft" pill>
Submit
</Button>
```

## Kbd
A key or a keyboard shortcut, such as ⌘K, set inline in text, in a tooltip or at the end of a menu item.
Import: import { Kbd } from "@plexui/ui/components/Kbd"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/kbd
Props:
  - size ("xs" | "sm" | "md") default: "sm" — Height and text size: 16px, 20px or 24px
  - variant ("soft" | "outline") default: "soft" — soft fills the key, outline draws its edge; both mix the text color
  - className (string) — Applied to the kbd element

### Overview
Kbd renders a {''} element: the semantic tag for keyboard input. It sits on the text baseline, so it can stand in a sentence.
```tsx
<p>
Press <Kbd>/</Kbd> to search, <Kbd>Esc</Kbd> to close.
</p>
```

### Shortcut
Use Kbd.Group for keys pressed together. Each key keeps its own frame.
```tsx
<Kbd.Group>
<Kbd>⌘</Kbd>
<Kbd>K</Kbd>
</Kbd.Group>

<Kbd.Group>
<Kbd>Ctrl</Kbd>
<Kbd>Shift</Kbd>
<Kbd>P</Kbd>
</Kbd.Group>
```

### Sizes and variants
Three sizes: xs (16px) for tooltips and menu items, sm (20px, default) for text, md (24px) next to larger controls. soft (default) fills the key, outline draws its edge. Both mix the surrounding text color, so a key reads on a page, in a dark tooltip and in a highlighted menu item alike.
```tsx
<Kbd size="xs">⌘K</Kbd>
<Kbd size="sm">⌘K</Kbd>
<Kbd size="md">⌘K</Kbd>

<Kbd variant="outline">⌘K</Kbd>
```

### In a tooltip and a menu
Show a control's shortcut in its tooltip, or at the end of a menu item. Kbd only shows the keys: announce the shortcut to assistive technology with aria-keyshortcuts on the control that has it.
```tsx
<Tooltip
content={
  <span className="flex items-center gap-2">
    Search
    <Kbd.Group>
      <Kbd size="xs">⌘</Kbd>
      <Kbd size="xs">K</Kbd>
    </Kbd.Group>
  </span>
}
>
<Button color="secondary" variant="outline" uniform aria-label="Search" aria-keyshortcuts="Meta+K">
  <Search />
</Button>
</Tooltip>

<Menu.Item onSelect={undo}>
<span className="flex-1">Undo</span>
<Kbd size="xs" variant="outline">⌘Z</Kbd>
</Menu.Item>
```

## Label
Accessible form label that points at any control by its id, so clicking it focuses or toggles the control, with consistent typography across forms.
Import: import { Label } from "@plexui/ui/components/Label"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/label
Props:
  - htmlFor (string) default: — — id of the associated control. Clicks on the label focus or activate the control.
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <label> element

### Overview
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
<Checkbox id="terms" />
<Label htmlFor="terms">Accept terms and conditions</Label>
</div>
```

### Label in Field
For stacked form rows with descriptions, errors, and horizontal layouts, use the Field component. It renders the label internally, hooks up htmlFor automatically, and handles the surrounding spacing.
```tsx
<Field label="Name on Card">
<Input placeholder="Aisha Cooper" />
</Field>

<Field label="Card Number" description="Enter your 16-digit card number">
<Input placeholder="1234 5678 9012 3456" />
</Field>

{/* Month / Year / CVV in a 3-col grid */}
{/* Billing Address section + checkbox */}
{/* Comments textarea + Submit / Cancel */}
```

## Markdown Editor
Compact rich text editor powered by Tiptap, embedded in a form field, with a markdown formatting toolbar, variants, and an invalid state.
Import: import { MarkdownEditor } from "@plexui/ui/components/MarkdownEditor"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/markdown-editor
Props:
  - variant ("outline" | "soft") default: "outline" — Visual style of the editor
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the editor
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Mark as invalid
  - placeholder (string) — Placeholder text when empty
  - value (string) — Controlled markdown value
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial markdown for uncontrolled mode
  - onChange ((markdown: string) => void) — Called on content change
  - toolbarEnd (ReactNode) — Content rendered at the end of the toolbar
  - rows (number) default: 1 — Minimum visible rows

### Placeholder
Use placeholder to display hint text when the editor is empty.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Enter text..." />
```

### All formatting
Example with all supported formatting: bold, italic, links, ordered lists, and unordered lists. Click inside formatted text to see toolbar buttons toggle.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor defaultValue={allFormattingMd} />
```

### With Field
Wrap with Field to add label, description, and error handling. The editor receives id and aria-describedby automatically.
```tsx
<Field label="Description" description="Supports bold, italic, lists, and links.">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Enter description..." />
</Field>
```

### Toolbar end slot
Use toolbarEnd to render custom content at the end of the toolbar, for example, an &ldquo;Edit translations&rdquo; button.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor
placeholder="Enter text..."
toolbarEnd={
  <button aria-label="Edit translations">
    <Translate />
  </button>
}
/>
```

### Variants
Use variant to switch between outline (default) and soft styles.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor variant="outline" />
<MarkdownEditor variant="soft" />
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to prevent editing and grey out the component.
```tsx
<MarkdownEditor disabled defaultValue="This content is **read-only**." />
```

### Invalid
Use invalid or wrap with Field and pass errorMessage to show an error state.
```tsx
<Field label="Bio" errorMessage="This field is required.">
<MarkdownEditor placeholder="Tell us about yourself..." invalid />
</Field>
```

## Markdown
Markdown renderer for rich formatted content, with headings, lists, tables, code blocks, and KaTeX math expressions out of the box.
Import: import { Markdown } from "@plexui/ui/components/Markdown"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/markdown
Props:
  - children (string) — Markdown source
  - includeMath (boolean) default: false — Enable LaTeX math rendering

### Overview
Use Markdown to render rich markdown text.
```tsx
<Markdown>{markdownContent}</Markdown>
```

### Math
Use includeMath to enable LaTeX rendering.
```tsx
<Markdown includeMath>{markdownWithLatex}</Markdown>
```

## Menu
Dropdown menu for structured actions with grouped items, submenus, checkbox and radio items, and horizontal layouts.
Import: import { Menu } from "@plexui/ui/components/Menu"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/menu
Props:
  - forceOpen (boolean) — Keep menu open (controlled)
  - onOpen (() => void) — Called when menu opens
  - onClose (() => void) — Called when menu closes
  - modal (boolean) — Whether menu is modal (focus trap)
  Menu.Content:
    - width (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Panel width in px
    - minWidth (number | "auto") default: 300 — Minimum panel width in px (vertical layout)
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") — Preferred placement
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") — Alignment relative to trigger
    - layout ("vertical" | "horizontal") default: "vertical" — Layout direction. Use horizontal for icon toolbars
    - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Size of horizontal menu items (icon size + padding)
  Menu.Item:
    - description (ReactNode) — Second line under the label. The label turns semibold on its own
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Called when item is selected
    - disabled (boolean) — Disable the item
    - danger (boolean) — Destructive action: the item is drawn in the danger color
  Menu.CheckboxItem:
    - checked (boolean | "indeterminate") — Checked state
    - onCheckedChange ((checked: boolean) => void) — When checkbox toggles
    - onSelect ((event: Event) => void) — Use with preventDefault() to keep menu open
    - indicatorPosition ("start" | "end") default: "end" — Checkbox position
    - indicatorVariant ("solid" | "ghost") default: "solid" — Checkbox indicator style

### Overview
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Sample menu <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content width={210} minWidth={210}>
  <Menu.Item description="sam.smith@gmail.com">Sam Smith</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Link href="/settings">Your profile</Menu.Link>
  <Menu.Link href="#">Terms & policies</Menu.Link>
  <Menu.Item disabled onSelect={() => {}}>Feature flags</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Logout</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Natural sizing
Menu supports several sizing strategies:Natural sizing: use minWidth="auto" to have the menu fit naturally to the size of the content.Fixed size: use width and minWidth to set the menu to a fixed size, regardless of content size.Flexible sizing: minWidth can be used by itself to describe a menu that must be a given size, but can grow larger depending on its content.Max sizing: apply max-width to the children of Menu.Content. maxWidth isn't exposed as a prop because it's reserved for Radix variables used in collision detection.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><Tools /> Tools</Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Functions height={18} width={18} /> Function</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Search height={18} width={18} /> File Search</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Globe height={18} width={18} /> Web Search</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Code height={18} width={18} /> Code Interpreter</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><ImageSquare height={18} width={18} /> Image Generation</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Horizontal (icons only)
Set layout="horizontal" on Menu.Content for an iOS-style icon toolbar.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Actions <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content layout="horizontal" minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EditPencil width={20} height={20} /></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><SettingsCog width={20} height={20} /></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Play width={20} height={20} /></Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><ExpandLg width={20} height={20} /></Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Horizontal (icons with labels)
Add text labels below icons for a labeled toolbar. The horizontal layout automatically stacks icon and text vertically within each item.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Actions <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content layout="horizontal" minWidth="auto">
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><EditPencil width={20} height={20} /> Edit</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><SettingsCog width={20} height={20} /> Settings</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><Play width={20} height={20} /> Play</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}><ExpandLg width={20} height={20} /> Expand</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Grouped items
Use Menu.Group and Menu.Label to organize related items into labeled sections.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><FileDocument /> Templates <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={220}>
  <Menu.Group>
    <Menu.Label>Active</Menu.Label>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Welcome email</Menu.Link>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Order confirmation</Menu.Link>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Password reset</Menu.Link>
  </Menu.Group>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Group>
    <Menu.Label>Draft</Menu.Label>
    <Menu.Link href="#">New promo campaign</Menu.Link>
    <Menu.Link href="#">Account deactivation</Menu.Link>
```
