```tsx
  </Menu.Group>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Submenus
Use Menu.Sub, Menu.SubTrigger, and Menu.SubContent for nested menus.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost">Options <ChevronDownMd /></Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content minWidth={180}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Edit</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Duplicate</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Sub>
    <Menu.SubTrigger>More</Menu.SubTrigger>
    <Menu.SubContent>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Move to project…</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Move to folder…</Menu.Item>
      <Menu.Separator />
      <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Advanced options…</Menu.Item>
    </Menu.SubContent>
  </Menu.Sub>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Share</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Add to favorites</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>Delete</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Checkbox items
Use Menu.CheckboxItem with checked, onCheckedChange, and {"onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}"} to keep the menu open.
```tsx
const [settings, setSettings] = useState({
showGrid: true,
showLabels: false,
enableShadows: false,
})

return (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <Button variant="ghost" color="primary">
      Checkbox menu <ChevronDownMd />
    </Button>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content minWidth={200}>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={settings.showGrid}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setSettings((s) => ({ ...s, showGrid: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      Show grid lines
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={settings.showLabels}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setSettings((s) => ({ ...s, showLabels: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      Display labels
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
    <Menu.CheckboxItem
      checked={settings.enableShadows}
      onCheckedChange={(checked) => setSettings((s) => ({ ...s, enableShadows: checked }))}
      onSelect={(evt) => evt.preventDefault()}
      indicatorPosition="end"
      indicatorVariant="solid"
    >
      Enable shadows
    </Menu.CheckboxItem>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)
```

### Radio items
Use Menu.RadioGroup and Menu.RadioItem for single-selection options.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("any")

<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" variant="ghost">
    Radio menu <ChevronDownMd />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="start" minWidth="auto" width="auto">
  <Menu.RadioGroup
    indicatorPosition="end"
    value={value}
    onChange={setValue}
  >
    <Menu.RadioItem value="any">Any time</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="today" disabled>Today</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last7d">Last 7 days</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last30d">Last 30 days</Menu.RadioItem>
    <Menu.RadioItem value="last3m">Last 3 months</Menu.RadioItem>
  </Menu.RadioGroup>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Item actions
Use Menu.ItemActions and Menu.ItemAction for hover actions (e.g. delete) on an item.Accessibility note: these actions are not keyboard accessible due to how Radix Menu works, so they should not be critical actions with no other parity.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="primary" size="lg" variant="ghost" className="font-semibold gap-1.5"><History /> Conversations</Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content width={270}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Sample thread title</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Another sample thread title</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={() => {}}>
    <span className="flex-1 truncate">Long thread title that is going to be clipped off</span>
    <Menu.ItemActions>
      <Menu.ItemAction onClick={() => {}}><Trash /></Menu.ItemAction>
    </Menu.ItemActions>
  </Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

### Destructive items
Mark a destructive action (delete, remove, leave) with danger: the label and the highlight take the danger color, and a description keeps its secondary color. Menu.Link takes danger too. Put such items last, after a separator.
```tsx
<Menu>
<Menu.Trigger>
  <Button color="secondary" variant="soft" uniform aria-label="More actions">
    <DotsHorizontal />
  </Button>
</Menu.Trigger>
<Menu.Content align="end" minWidth={200}>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={rename}><EditPencil /> Rename</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Item onSelect={duplicate}>Duplicate</Menu.Item>
  <Menu.Separator />
  <Menu.Item onSelect={remove} danger><Trash /> Delete project</Menu.Item>
</Menu.Content>
</Menu>
```

## OTP Input
Input for one-time passwords and verification codes, with split digit cells, grouped layouts, error states, and autofill.
Import: import { OTPInput } from "@plexui/ui/components/OTPInput"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/otp-input
Props:
  - length (number) default: 6 — Number of digit cells
  - value (string) — Controlled value
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when value changes
  - onComplete ((value: string) => void) — Called when all digits filled
  - grouping (number[]) — Grouping pattern with extra gap (e.g. [3,3])
  - invalid (boolean) default: false — Invalid visual state
  - errorMessage (string) — Error message below the input
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable all cells
  - autoFocus (boolean) default: false — Auto-focus first cell on mount

### Overview
```tsx
<OTPInput />
```

### Filled state
```tsx
<OTPInput value="488030" onChange={setValue} />
```

### Grouped (3+3)
```tsx
<OTPInput grouping={[3, 3]} />
```

### With error
```tsx
<OTPInput invalid errorMessage="Invalid verification code." />
```

### Disabled
```tsx
<OTPInput value="488030" disabled />
```

## Popover
A floating panel for contextual UI, with flexible sizing, hover triggers, a controllable open state and nesting.
Import: import { Popover } from "@plexui/ui/components/Popover"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/popover
Props:
  - showOnHover (boolean) — Open on hover and focus instead of click
  Popover.Content:
    - width (number | "auto") default: "auto" — Panel width in px
    - minWidth (number | "auto") default: 300 — Minimum panel width in px
    - maxWidth (number) — Maximum panel width in px
    - side ("top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left") — Preferred placement
    - align ("start" | "center" | "end") — Alignment relative to trigger
    - sideOffset (number) — Offset from trigger (px)
    - alignOffset (number) — Alignment offset (px)

### Overview
```tsx
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger><Button color="primary">Generate</Button></Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content side="right">...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Sizing the popover
The popover can be sized with any combination of width, minWidth, or maxWidth. All popovers default to a minWidth of 300px, and a maxWidth of Radix's viewport detection.
```tsx
<Popover>
<Popover.Trigger>...</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth="auto" side="top">...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Open on hover
Use showOnHover to create popovers that appear on hover and focus events. This should be used sparingly and with clear intention.By default, hover popovers will not alter the focused element on the page, nor restore focus to the trigger on close. However, if interactive content is present in the popover, and tab is used to navigate into the popover, focus will be restored to the trigger on close.
```tsx
<Popover showOnHover>
<Popover.Trigger>...</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content>...</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

### Using the controller
You can access usePopoverController() controller context from components within Popover.Content. The hook exposes two methods, close() and shake(). They do exactly what you think they do.Attempting to submit an empty form calls the shake() methodAfter async submission occurs (faked loading state), the close() method is called to close the popup imperatively.
```tsx
const { close, shake } = usePopoverController()
// e.g. close after form submit, shake on validation error
```

## Progress Steps
Stepper for multi-step flows like checkouts and onboarding, with horizontal or vertical layout, icons, navigation, and color tokens.
Import: import { ProgressSteps } from "@plexui/ui/components/ProgressSteps"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/progress-steps
Props:
  - current (number) — Current active step (1-based)
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction
  - size ("sm" | "md" | "lg") default: "md" — Step indicator size
  - color ("default" | "success") default: "default" — Color scheme for completed/active steps
  - connectorStyle ("solid" | "dashed") default: "solid" — Connector line style
  - variant ("default" | "minimal") default: "default" — "minimal" renders a compact bar (requires total)
  - total (number) — Total steps for minimal variant
  ProgressSteps.Step:
    - icon (ReactNode) — Custom icon instead of step number

### Overview
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2}>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Your details</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Please provide your name and email</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Company details</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>A few details about your company</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Invite your team</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Start collaborating with your team</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step>
  <ProgressSteps.Title>Add your socials</ProgressSteps.Title>
  <ProgressSteps.Description>Share posts to your social accounts</ProgressSteps.Description>
</ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Sizes
Use size to control the scale of step indicators.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2} size="md">
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 1</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 2</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 3</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step><ProgressSteps.Title>Step 4</ProgressSteps.Title></ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Vertical
Use orientation="vertical" to display steps in a vertical layout, ideal for sidebar navigation or multi-step forms. The example also shows the dashed connector style.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2} orientation="vertical">...</ProgressSteps>
<ProgressSteps current={3} orientation="vertical" connectorStyle="dashed">...</ProgressSteps>
```

### With Icons
Use icon prop on ProgressSteps.Step to display custom icons instead of step numbers.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={3}>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Email />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Globe />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Users />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
<ProgressSteps.Step icon={<Bolt />}>...</ProgressSteps.Step>
</ProgressSteps>
```

### With Navigation
Example of integrating with navigation controls.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps variant="minimal" current={step} total={4} />
<Button onClick={() => setStep(s => Math.max(1, s - 1))}>Previous</Button>
<Button onClick={() => setStep(s => Math.min(4, s + 1))}>Next</Button>
```

### Minimal
Use variant="minimal" for a compact horizontal bar indicator. Requires total prop.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps variant="minimal" current={3} total={4} color="default" />
```

### Icons Only
Omit Title and Description for a minimal indicator when step details are shown elsewhere.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={2}>
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
<ProgressSteps.Step />
</ProgressSteps>
```

### Colors
Use color to change the color scheme of completed and active steps.
```tsx
<ProgressSteps current={3}>...</ProgressSteps>
<ProgressSteps current={3} color="success">...</ProgressSteps>
```

## Progress
A horizontal bar that shows task completion, with determinate and indeterminate modes, labelled layouts, and smooth value transitions.
Import: import { Progress } from "@plexui/ui/components/Progress"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/progress
Props:
  - value (number | null) default: null — Current progress between 0 and max. Pass null for indeterminate.
  - max (number) default: 100 — Maximum progress value
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(13);
useEffect(() => {
const t = setTimeout(() => setValue(66), 500);
return () => clearTimeout(t);
}, []);

return <Progress value={value} aria-label="Loading" />;
```

### With label
Pair a Label with a value readout above the bar, the typical upload / onboarding progress pattern.
```tsx
<div>
<div style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <Label id="progress-upload-label">Uploading plex-ui.zip</Label>
  <span>3.2 / 4.8 MB</span>
</div>
<Progress aria-labelledby="progress-upload-label" value={67} />
</div>
```

### Controlled
Bind value to any source. Here it follows a Slider.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(50);

return (
<>
  <Progress value={value} aria-label="Progress" />
  <Slider value={value} onChange={setValue} min={0} max={100} step={1} aria-label="Progress value" />
</>
);
```

## Radio Group
Radio group for single-choice selection with row or column layout, right-aligned indicators, rich item content, and card-style options.
Import: import { RadioGroup } from "@plexui/ui/components/RadioGroup"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/radio-group
Props:
  - value (string) — Controlled selected value
  - defaultValue (string) — Initial selected value (uncontrolled)
  - onChange ((value: string) => void) — Called when selected option changes
  - direction ("col" | "row") default: "row" — Item flow direction
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable the whole group
  - aria-label (string) — Accessible group label
  RadioGroup.Item:
    - value (string) — Item value
    - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable this item only
    - block (boolean) default: false — Stretch item to fill available width
    - orientation ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Position of the radio indicator relative to the label
    - description (ReactNode) — Second line below the option's label, linked via aria-describedby

### Overview
```tsx
const [frequency, setFrequency] = useState("daily")
<RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Notification frequency">
<RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Checkbox
Place RadioGroup alongside Checkbox controls to verify that indicator sizes, label baselines, and spacing align consistently in both horizontal and vertical layouts.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6 w-full max-w-md">
<Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
  {() => (
    <RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Notification channel">
      <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="sms">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">SMS</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Text messages to your phone number.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
      <RadioGroup.Item value="push">
        <div className="flex flex-col">
          <span className="font-medium">Push</span>
          <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Real-time alerts on your device.</span>
        </div>
      </RadioGroup.Item>
    </RadioGroup>
  )}
</Field>
<Field label="Topics" description="Select the topics you want to follow.">
  {() => (
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2.5">
      <Checkbox defaultChecked label={...} />
      ...
    </div>
  )}
</Field>
</div>
```

### Descriptions
Combine Field-level label and description with item-level descriptions for options that need additional context. Use a plain label without descriptions when the options are self-explanatory.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Notification channel" description="Choose how you'd like to be notified.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={channel} onChange={setChannel} aria-label="Notification channel">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="email">
          <div className="flex flex-col">
            <span className="font-medium">Email</span>
            <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">Messages delivered to your inbox.</span>
          </div>
        </RadioGroup.Item>
        ...
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Notification frequency">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Notification frequency">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

### Direction
Use direction to control whether the items flow in a column or row. An optimal gap will be dynamically applied based on the orientation.
```tsx
<RadioGroup direction="col" defaultValue="light" aria-label="Theme">
<RadioGroup.Item value="light">Light</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="dark">Dark</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="system">System</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Orientation
Use orientation="right" on RadioGroup.Item to place the radio indicator after the label text. Useful for settings lists and card-style selections where the content should lead.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="w-[320px]" direction="col" defaultValue="email" aria-label="Default notification channel">
<RadioGroup.Item value="email" orientation="right" block>Email</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="sms" orientation="right" block>SMS</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="push" orientation="right" block>Push notification</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Group disabled
Use disabled on RadioGroup to disable all radio options.
```tsx
<RadioGroup disabled defaultValue="standard" aria-label="Shipping method">
<RadioGroup.Item value="standard">Standard</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="express">Express</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="overnight">Overnight</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### Item disabled
Use disabled on single RadioGroup.Item to disable only that option.
```tsx
<RadioGroup aria-label="Delivery method" direction="col">
<RadioGroup.Item value="standard">Standard shipping (3–5 days)</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="express" disabled>Express shipping (1–2 days)</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="same-day">
  Same-day delivery — available in select metro areas with a minimum order of $50
</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With description
Use description on an item for a second line under its label. It sits outside the label, so the radio keeps the label as its name and gets the description through aria-describedby; clicking it does not select the option.
```tsx
<RadioGroup direction="col" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Spacing">
<RadioGroup.Item value="default" description="Standard spacing for most use cases.">
  Default
</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="comfortable" description="More space between elements.">
  Comfortable
</RadioGroup.Item>
<RadioGroup.Item value="compact" description="Minimal spacing for dense layouts.">
  Compact
</RadioGroup.Item>
</RadioGroup>
```

### With Field
Wrap a RadioGroup in a Field for a shared label and description. The Field provides aria-describedby linking automatically.
```tsx
<Field label="Notification method" description="Choose how you want to receive notifications.">
{() => (
  <RadioGroup direction="col" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Notification method">
    <RadioGroup.Item value="email">Email</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="sms">SMS</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="push">Push notification</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>
```

### With Field error
When a Field has an errorMessage, it sets aria-invalid on the child control for screen readers. The error message is displayed below the group.
```tsx
<Field
label="Subscription plan"
description="Select a plan to continue."
errorMessage={showError ? "Please select a subscription plan." : undefined}
>
{(fieldProps) => (
  <RadioGroup direction="col" aria-label="Subscription plan" {...fieldProps}>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly ($9.99/month)</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="yearly">Yearly ($99.99/year)</RadioGroup.Item>
    <RadioGroup.Item value="lifetime">Lifetime ($299.99)</RadioGroup.Item>
  </RadioGroup>
)}
</Field>
```

### Choice card
Style each radio option as a bordered card with visual selection state. The selected card gets a highlighted border using design tokens. Use orientation="right" to place the indicator after the content. Wrap each RadioGroup.Item in a card container with border and borderRadius on the same element.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="flex-col w-[320px] gap-3" value={value} onChange={setValue} aria-label="Workspace type">
<div style={{
  border: "1px solid",
  borderColor: isSelected ? "var(--color-background-primary-solid)" : "var(--color-border-primary-outline)",
  borderRadius: "var(--radius-lg)",
  backgroundColor: isSelected ? "var(--color-background-primary-soft-alpha)" : undefined,
}}>
  <RadioGroup.Item value="personal" block orientation={orientation} className="gap-3 p-3">
    <div className="flex flex-col flex-1">
      <span className="font-semibold">Personal</span>
      <span className="text-xs text-secondary mt-0.5">For hobby projects and experimentation.</span>
    </div>
  </RadioGroup.Item>
</div>
...
</RadioGroup>
```

### Card selection
Leverage component composition and className overrides to build card-style radio selections with rich content per option.
```tsx
<RadioGroup className="flex-col w-[390px] gap-4">
<RadioGroup.Item className="gap-2.5" value="basic">
  <div><h4>Basic Plan</h4><p className="text-secondary text-sm">5 GB storage</p></div>
</RadioGroup.Item>
...
</RadioGroup>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate radio groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col max-w-sm w-full divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Visibility" description="Control who can see project resources.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={visibility} onChange={setVisibility} aria-label="Visibility">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="hidden">Hidden</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="owners">Visible to organization owners</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="everyone">Visible to everyone</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Digest frequency" description="How often you receive summary emails.">
    {() => (
      <RadioGroup direction="col" value={frequency} onChange={setFrequency} aria-label="Digest frequency">
        <RadioGroup.Item value="daily">Daily</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="weekly">Weekly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="monthly">Monthly</RadioGroup.Item>
        <RadioGroup.Item value="never">Never</RadioGroup.Item>
      </RadioGroup>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

## Select Control
Select control primitive for building custom dropdowns, with variants, sizing, start and dropdown icons, and clearable, loading, and invalid states.
Import: import { SelectControl } from "@plexui/ui/components/SelectControl"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/select-control
Props:
  - selected (boolean) — Whether a value is selected (affects placeholder styling)
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Visual variant
  - size (ControlSize) — Control size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) — Fully rounded trigger
  - StartIcon (Component) — Icon at start
  - onClearClick (() => void) — Enables clear button when set
  - dropdownIconType ("chevronDown" | "dropdown" | "none") — Dropdown indicator style
  - invalid (boolean) — Invalid state
  - disabled (boolean) — Disable control
  - block (boolean) — Full width
  - loading (boolean) — Loading state
  - opticallyAlign ("start" | "end") — Optical alignment

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState("")
const placeholder = "Select date..."

return (
<Menu>
  <Menu.Trigger>
    <SelectControl selected={!!value} onClearClick={() => setValue("")} StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>
      {value || placeholder}
    </SelectControl>
  </Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Content>
    <Menu.RadioGroup value={value} onChange={setValue}>
      ...
    </Menu.RadioGroup>
  </Menu.Content>
</Menu>
)
```

### Variants
Use the variant prop to stylize the select control. Available variant styles are similar to {""}, but aligned with subtle differences from {""} variant treatments.
```tsx
<SelectControl variant="soft" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
<SelectControl variant="outline" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
<SelectControl variant="ghost" selected StartIcon={Cabinet} onClearClick={() => {}}>Sample value</SelectControl>
```

### Sizing & roundness
Sizing of the control is determined with the size prop. Each size provides dynamic values for various aspects of the control, including icon and indicator placement, as well font-size and gutter values.Create fully rounded controls with the pill prop. When pill is set, extra horizontal gutter is dynamically applied, and the clear action is also set to pill.
```tsx
<SelectControl size="md" pill={false} dropdownIconType="none">Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md" loading>Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md">Select...</SelectControl>
<SelectControl size="md" StartIcon={Tools} dropdownIconType="none">Tool calls</SelectControl>
...
```

### Selected
Use selected to indicate if the control has a selected value, which toggles visual placeholder styling.As you'll notice here, this doesn't do anything to the content of the control. That's up to you.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected={false}>Select...</SelectControl>
```

### Start icon
Use StartIcon to display an icon in the control. Sizing, spacing, and coloring are handled automatically.
```tsx
<SelectControl StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select date...</SelectControl>
```

### Dropdown icon
Use dropdownIconType to control the presentation of the dropdown indicator.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected dropdownIconType="dropdown" StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>Select...</SelectControl>
```

### Clearable
Pass a callback onClearClick to enable the clearable action.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected onClearClick={() => setValue("")} StartIcon={CalendarAlt}>
{value || "Select..."}
</SelectControl>
```

### Loading
During loading, dropdown icon and clear actions are automatically hidden.Interactions will be prevented by default during this state, by providing a default value for inert to true. You can override this behavior directly with inert, or use disabled to add visual disablement.
```tsx
<SelectControl loading>Loading models...</SelectControl>
```

### Invalid
Use invalid to visually indicate the control is in an invalid state.
```tsx
<SelectControl invalid selected>Pineapple on pizza</SelectControl>
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to both visually and accessibly disable the control.
```tsx
<SelectControl disabled selected StartIcon={User}>Reader</SelectControl>
```

### Block
Create full-width controls with the block prop.
```tsx
<div className="w-[290px] text-center p-2 border border-dashed border-alpha/20 rounded-md">
<SelectControl block size="lg">Select...</SelectControl>
</div>
```

### Country selector
A plain country selector built with Select. Shows flag icons with country names, no dial codes. Useful for profile forms, shipping addresses, and other country-only fields.
```tsx
const countries = [
{ value: "us", label: "United States" },
{ value: "gb", label: "United Kingdom" },
// ...60 countries
];

const CountryView = ({ value }) => (
<span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <img src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${value}.svg`} width={20} />
  {countries.find(c => c.value === value)?.label}
</span>
);

<Select
value={country}
options={countries}
onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
placeholder="Select country..."
size="lg"
block
searchable
TriggerView={CountryView}
listMinWidth={300}
/>
```

### Country code selector
A searchable country selector built with Select. Custom TriggerView and OptionView render flag icons and dial codes. Search matches both country name and dial code.
```tsx
const countries = [
{ value: "us", label: "United States (+1)", dialCode: "+1" },
{ value: "gb", label: "United Kingdom (+44)", dialCode: "+44" },
// ...60 countries
];

const CountryTriggerView = ({ value }) => {
const country = lookup.get(value);
return (
  <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
    <img src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${value}.svg`} width={20} />
    {country.label} ({country.dialCode})
  </span>
);
};

<Select
value={country}
options={countries}
onChange={(option) => setCountry(option.value)}
placeholder="Select country..."
size="lg"
block
searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
TriggerView={CountryTriggerView}
listMinWidth={300}
/>
```

### Phone form
Country selector with flag icons and phone input composed into a form. Selecting a country updates the dial code prefix and clears the phone field. Phone numbers are formatted as you type using per-country patterns (e.g. 123 456 7890 for US, 1234 567 890 for UK). Search works by both country name and dial code. Validation runs on submit: the phone field shows an error state with FieldError when the number is too short or too long.
```tsx
import { useState, useCallback, useRef } from 'react';
import { Input } from '@plexui/ui/components/Input';
import { Select, type Option } from '@plexui/ui/components/Select';
import { Button } from '@plexui/ui/components/Button';
import { FieldError } from '@plexui/ui/components/FieldError';

// Country data — include all 245 countries in production
type Country = { value: string; label: string; dialCode: string; flag: string };

const COUNTRIES: Country[] = [
{ value: 'us', label: 'United States', dialCode: '+1', flag: '🇺🇸' },
{ value: 'gb', label: 'United Kingdom', dialCode: '+44', flag: '🇬🇧' },
{ value: 'de', label: 'Germany', dialCode: '+49', flag: '🇩🇪' },
{ value: 'fr', label: 'France', dialCode: '+33', flag: '🇫🇷' },
{ value: 'es', label: 'Spain', dialCode: '+34', flag: '🇪🇸' },
{ value: 'it', label: 'Italy', dialCode: '+39', flag: '🇮🇹' },
{ value: 'jp', label: 'Japan', dialCode: '+81', flag: '🇯🇵' },
{ value: 'au', label: 'Australia', dialCode: '+61', flag: '🇦🇺' },
{ value: 'br', label: 'Brazil', dialCode: '+55', flag: '🇧🇷' },
{ value: 'in', label: 'India', dialCode: '+91', flag: '🇮🇳' },
// ... full list of 245 countries
];

const COUNTRY_LOOKUP = new Map(COUNTRIES.map((c) => [c.value, c]));
const COUNTRY_OPTIONS = COUNTRIES.map((c) => ({
...c,
label: `${c.label} (${c.dialCode})`,
}));

// Per-country phone number format patterns
const PHONE_FORMATS: Record<string, number[]> = {
us: [3, 3, 4], ca: [3, 3, 4],   // 123 456 7890
gb: [4, 3, 3], de: [3, 4, 4],   // 1234 567 890 | 123 4567 8901
fr: [1, 2, 2, 2, 2],            // 1 23 45 67 89
es: [3, 2, 2, 2],               // 123 45 67 89
it: [3, 3, 4], jp: [2, 4, 4],
au: [3, 3, 3], br: [2, 5, 4],
in: [5, 5],                      // 12345 67890
// ... add more countries as needed
};

function formatPhoneNumber(raw: string, countryCode?: string) {
const digits = raw.replace(/\D/g, '');
if (!digits) return '';
const format = (countryCode && PHONE_FORMATS[countryCode]) || [3, 3, 4];
const groups: string[] = [];
let i = 0;
for (const size of format) {
  if (i >= digits.length) break;
  groups.push(digits.slice(i, i + size));
  i += size;
}
if (i < digits.length) groups.push(digits.slice(i));
return groups.join(' ');
}

// Flag icon — SVG flags from lipis/flag-icons, all 4:3
function FlagIcon({ code, trigger }: { code: string; trigger?: boolean }) {
return (
  <span
    style={{
      display: 'block',
      height: trigger ? 'var(--start-icon-size, 18px)' : 16,
      aspectRatio: '4 / 3',
      borderRadius: 2,
      overflow: 'hidden',
      flexShrink: 0,
    }}
  >
    <img
      src={`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/lipis/flag-icons@7.5.0/flags/4x3/${code}.svg`}
      alt=""
      loading="lazy"
      style={{
        display: 'block',
        width: '100%',
        height: '100%',
      }}
    />
  </span>
);
}

// Custom trigger and option renderers
const CountryTriggerView = ({ value }: Option) => {
const country = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(value);
if (!country) return null;
return (
  <span style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, height: '100%' }}>
    <FlagIcon code={value} trigger />
    {country.label} ({country.dialCode})
  </span>
);
};

const CountryOptionView = ({ value, label }: Option) => (
<span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8 }}>
  <FlagIcon code={value} />
  {label}
</span>
);

// Search matches country name or dial code
const searchPredicate = (option: Option, term: string) => {
const country = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(option.value);
if (!country) return false;
return (
  country.label.toLowerCase().includes(term) ||
  country.dialCode.includes(term)
);
};

function PhoneForm() {
const [country, setCountry] = useState('us');
const [phone, setPhone] = useState('');
const [submitted, setSubmitted] = useState(false);
const phoneRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);

const dialCode = COUNTRY_LOOKUP.get(country)?.dialCode ?? '+1';
const digits = phone.replace(/\D/g, '');
const isValid = digits.length >= 7 && digits.length <= 15;
const showError = submitted && !isValid;

const handleCountryChange = useCallback((option: Option) => {
  setCountry(option.value);
  setPhone('');
  setSubmitted(false);
  setTimeout(() => phoneRef.current?.focus(), 0);
}, []);

const handlePhoneChange = useCallback(
  (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    setPhone(formatPhoneNumber(e.target.value.replace(/\D/g, ''), country));
    setSubmitted(false);
  },
  [country]
);

return (
  <form onSubmit={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setSubmitted(true); }} noValidate>
    <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
      <Select
        value={country}
        options={COUNTRY_OPTIONS}
        onChange={handleCountryChange}
        placeholder="Select country..."
        size="lg"
        block
        searchPlaceholder="Search countries..."
        searchPredicate={searchPredicate}
        TriggerView={CountryTriggerView}
        OptionView={CountryOptionView}
        listMinWidth={300}
      />
      <div>
        <Input
          ref={phoneRef}
          value={phone}
          onChange={handlePhoneChange}
          placeholder="Phone number"
          type="tel"
          inputMode="tel"
          size="lg"
          invalid={showError}
          startAdornment={
            <span className="text-tertiary whitespace-nowrap select-none">
              {dialCode}
            </span>
          }
        />
        {showError && (
      <FieldError className="mt-1.5">Phone number is not valid.</FieldError>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
<Button type="submit" color="primary" variant="solid" size="lg" className="w-full mt-3">
      Continue
    </Button>
  </form>
);
}
```

### Optical alignment
Use opticallyAlign with either "start" or "end" to offset the gutter of the control.
```tsx
<SelectControl selected variant="ghost" opticallyAlign="start">Ghost control</SelectControl>
```

## Select
Select dropdown with grouped options, per-item descriptions, multiple selection, action items, and column-based layouts.
Import: import { Select } from "@plexui/ui/components/Select"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/select
Props:
  - options (Options<T>) — Array of options or grouped options
  - value (string | string[]) — Selected value (single) or values (multiple)
  - onChange (function) — Called when selection changes
  - multiple (boolean) default: false — Allow multiple selection
  - placeholder (string) default: "Select..." — Trigger placeholder
  - variant ("soft" | "outline" | "ghost") default: "outline" — Trigger variant
  - size (ControlSize) default: "md" — Trigger size (3xs to 3xl)
  - pill (boolean) default: false — Rounded trigger
  - clearable (boolean) default: false — Show clear button
  - block (boolean) default: variant !== "ghost" — Full width trigger
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable select
  - actions (array) — Actions below options list
  - checkPosition ("start" | "end" | "none") default: "start" — Where the check indicator sits in the list. "none" removes the indicator column for lists that never carry a selection
  - OptionView (React.FC) — Custom option render
  - TriggerView (React.FC) — Custom trigger render (multi)
  - searchPlaceholder (string) — Search input placeholder
  - searchAriaLabel (string) default: "Search options" — Accessible name of the search input, independent of the trigger label
  - searchSize (ControlSize) default: "md" — Size of the search input in the menu, such as 2xl for 44px touch targets on phones

### Overview
```tsx
<Select
value={fruit}
options={fruits}
onChange={handleChange}
placeholder="Select a fruit..."
variant="solid"
/>
```

### With descriptions
Options carrying a description field render a secondary line under each label. The title stays semibold in every state (idle, highlighted, selected). The component handles that automatically, no optionClassName needed. Use TriggerStartIcon to reflect the selected option's identity in the trigger.
```tsx
const RoleOptionDescription = ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) => (
<div className="font-normal text-secondary text-[0.935em] leading-[1.45]">
  {children}
</div>
);

const roles = [
{
  value: "owner",
  label: "Owner",
  description: (
    <RoleOptionDescription>
      Can modify project information and manage project members
    </RoleOptionDescription>
  ),
},
{
  value: "reader",
  label: "Reader",
  description: (
    <RoleOptionDescription>
      Can make API requests that read or modify data
    </RoleOptionDescription>
  ),
},
];

<Select
value={role}
options={roles}
placeholder="Select role..."
align="start"
listMinWidth={260}
variant="ghost"
size="lg"
onChange={({ value }) => setRole(value)}
TriggerStartIcon={role === "owner" ? UserLock : User}
/>
```

### Actions
Custom, arbitrary actions can be displayed below the options list via the actions prop.
```tsx
<Select
value={value}
onChange={handleChange}
options={items}
placeholder="Select..."
align="start"
listMinWidth={240}
actions={[
  { id: "create", label: "Create project", Icon: Plus, onSelect: () => {} },
  { id: "overview", label: "Organization overview", Icon: Workspace, onSelect: () => {} },
]}
/>
```

### Grouped options
Select supports option groups, similar to the native &lt;optgroup&gt; element. All selects are searchable by default, but will only present a searchbox when it makes sense. Currently, this means when there are 15 or more options.
```tsx
<Select
value={value}
options={groupedItems}
onChange={(v) => setValue(v.value)}
variant="outline"
size="lg"
side="bottom"
listMinWidth={300}
searchPlaceholder="Select an option..."
clearable
/>
```

### Multiple selection
Multiple selection is supported through the multiple property. This changes how value, onChange, and TriggerView are typed, accepting and returning arrays of values.
```tsx
<Select
variant="soft"
placeholder="Select fruits..."
options={fruitsOptions}
name="fruits"
multiple
clearable
value={fruits}
onChange={(values) => setFruits(values.map(({ value }) => value))}
TriggerView={MultiFruitTriggerView}
/>
```

### Column configuration
A column-visibility panel built with Popover and Switch. Toggling a switch moves the column between shown and hidden groups.
```tsx
const [shown, setShown] = useState(['name', 'email', 'role', 'status'])
const toggle = (id) => {
setShown((prev) =>
  prev.includes(id) ? prev.filter((c) => c !== id) : [...prev, id]
)
}
const shownColumns = allColumns.filter((c) => shown.includes(c.id))
const hiddenColumns = allColumns.filter((c) => !shown.includes(c.id))
<Popover.Trigger>
  <Button variant="outline" size="sm"><SettingsSlider /> Columns</Button>
</Popover.Trigger>
<Popover.Content minWidth={240} side="bottom" align="start">
  {shownColumns.map((col) => (
    <Row key={col.id} onClick={() => toggle(col.id)}>
      <span>{col.label}</span>
      <Switch checked />
    </Row>
  ))}
  {hiddenColumns.map((col) => (
    <Row key={col.id} onClick={() => toggle(col.id)}>
      <span className="text-tertiary">{col.label}</span>
      <Switch checked={false} />
    </Row>
  ))}
</Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

## Separator
A thin divider between content, horizontal or vertical, decorative by default or exposed to assistive technology when it marks a real grouping.
Import: import { Separator } from "@plexui/ui/components/Separator"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/separator
Props:
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Direction of the divider
  - decorative (boolean) default: true — When true, the separator is ignored by assistive technologies. Set false when the divider carries semantic grouping (renders role="separator").
  - className (string) default: — — Applied to the root <div>

### Overview
```tsx
<div>
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Aisha Cooper</div>
  <div className="text-muted">Engineering · Platform team</div>
</div>
<Separator />
<div>Shipped 24 pull requests this week across CI/CD and developer tooling.</div>
</div>
```

### Vertical
Use orientation="vertical" between inline items. Works for meta-strips, breadcrumbs, and dot-less separators.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', height: 20, alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
<div>MIT license</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>12k weekly downloads</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>48 kB bundle</div>
</div>
```

### Menu
Vertical separators between menu items with a short caption underneath each label.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 16 }}>
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Starter</div>
  <div className="text-muted">Free · 1 project</div>
</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Pro</div>
  <div className="text-muted">$19/mo · Unlimited</div>
</div>
<Separator orientation="vertical" />
<div>
  <div style={{ fontWeight: 500 }}>Enterprise</div>
  <div className="text-muted">Custom · Priority SLA</div>
</div>
</div>
```

### List
Horizontal separators between rows in a definition list.
```tsx
<div style={{ display: 'flex', flexDirection: 'column', gap: 8, maxWidth: 384 }}>
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Version</dt><dd>0.9.0</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Published</dt><dd>2 days ago</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>Bundle</dt><dd>48 kB</dd>
</dl>
<Separator />
<dl style={{ display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'space-between' }}>
  <dt>License</dt><dd>MIT</dd>
</dl>
</div>
```

## Shimmer Text
Text with a shimmer animation for loading and in-progress states, always on or toggled with a graceful stop.
Import: import { ShimmerText, ShimmerableText } from "@plexui/ui/components/ShimmerText"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/shimmer-text
Props:
  - as ("p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "div") default: "div" — HTML element to render
  - children (ReactNode) — Text content to shimmer
  - className (string) — Additional CSS classes
  ShimmerableText:
    - as ("p" | "span" | "h1" | "h2" | "h3" | "h4" | "h5" | "h6" | "div") default: "div" — HTML element to render
    - shimmer (boolean) default: false — Whether the shimmer animation is active
    - children (ReactNode) — Text content to shimmer
    - className (string) — Additional CSS classes

### Overview
ShimmerText applies a continuous shimmer animation to text content. Useful for loading states, AI-generated content indicators, or visual emphasis.
```tsx
<ShimmerText className="text-lg font-semibold">
Thinking...
</ShimmerText>
```

### Semantic elements
Use the as prop to render as any text element: p, span, h1 to h6, or div.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<ShimmerText as="h2" className="text-2xl font-bold">Heading shimmer</ShimmerText>
<ShimmerText as="p" className="text-base">Paragraph shimmer effect</ShimmerText>
<ShimmerText as="span" className="text-sm text-secondary">Inline shimmer</ShimmerText>
</div>
```

### Controllable shimmer
ShimmerableText allows toggling the shimmer on and off. When shimmer is set to false, the animation finishes its current iteration and then pauses gracefully, with no abrupt cut. Use this variant when text transitions between a loading and idle state.
```tsx
const [shimmer, setShimmer] = useState(true)

<ShimmerableText shimmer={shimmer} className="text-lg font-semibold">
Generating response...
</ShimmerableText>
```

## Sidebar
Composable navigation sidebar for app shells with collapsible sections, search and filter, tree views with hover actions, and a mobile menu
Import: import { SidebarProvider, SidebarLayout, Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarContent, SidebarFooter, SidebarGroup, SidebarGroupLabel, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarInset, SidebarTrigger } from "@plexui/ui/components/Sidebar"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/sidebar
Props:
  - variant ("sidebar" | "docs") default: "sidebar" — Visual variant
  - side ("left" | "right") default: "left" — Which side the sidebar is on
  SidebarProvider:
    - collapsible ("offcanvas" | "icon" | "none") default: "offcanvas" — Collapse behavior: offcanvas (drawer on mobile, full collapse on desktop), icon (icon rail), or none
    - defaultOpen (boolean) default: true — Initial open state (uncontrolled)
    - open (boolean) — Controlled open state
    - onOpenChange ((open: boolean) => void) — Called when open state changes
  SidebarMenuButton:
    - isActive (boolean) default: false — Highlight the current page
    - tooltip (string | ReactNode) — Label shown on hover when collapsed (icon mode). Hidden on mobile.
  SidebarGroupLabel:
    - size ("sm" | "lg") default: "lg" — sm: compact, tertiary. lg: larger, primary, more spacing
  SidebarMenuSub:
    - open (boolean) default: true — Whether submenu is expanded
    - hasIcons (boolean) default: false — Align child items with parent text that has icons
  SidebarCard:
    - dismissible (boolean) — Shows dismiss button
    - onDismiss (() => void) — Callback when dismissed

### App Shell
A multi-section app shell with a workspace selector, expandable parent sections with sub-items, and a footer with a documentation link plus a user menu. When collapsed (icon mode), hovering a parent icon opens a Popover flyout listing the section&apos;s items so users keep one-click access without expanding the rail.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="icon">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 600 }}>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <span>Console</span>
      <SidebarTrigger />
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      {/* Workspace selector */}
      <SidebarMenuItem>
        <Menu>
          <Menu.Trigger>
            <SidebarMenuButton tooltip="Default workspace">
              <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Cube /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
              <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Default</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              <ChevronUpDown className="ml-auto" />
            </SidebarMenuButton>
          </Menu.Trigger>
          <Menu.Content>...</Menu.Content>
        </Menu>
      </SidebarMenuItem>

      {/* Parent section: hover flyout when collapsed */}
      {state === "collapsed" ? (
        <Popover showOnHover>
          <Popover.Trigger>
            <SidebarMenuButton>
              <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><SettingsWrench /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
              <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Build</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              <SidebarMenuChevron />
            </SidebarMenuButton>
          </Popover.Trigger>
          <Popover.Content side="right" minWidth={220}>
            <div>Build / Workbench / Files / Skills / Batches</div>
          </Popover.Content>
        </Popover>
      ) : (
        <SidebarMenuItem expanded={isExpanded}>
          <SidebarMenuButton onClick={toggle}>
            <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><SettingsWrench /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Build</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
            <SidebarMenuChevron />
          </SidebarMenuButton>
          <SidebarMenuSub open={isExpanded} hasIcons>
            <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={1}>Workbench</SidebarMenuSubButton>
            ...
          </SidebarMenuSub>
        </SidebarMenuItem>
      )}
    </SidebarContent>
    <SidebarFooter>
      <SidebarMenuButton><Book /> Documentation</SidebarMenuButton>
      <Menu>
        <Menu.Trigger>
          <SidebarMenuButton>
            <Avatar name="Alex" />
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Alex · Admin</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
          </SidebarMenuButton>
        </Menu.Trigger>
        <Menu.Content>...</Menu.Content>
      </Menu>
    </SidebarFooter>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Basic
```tsx
<SidebarProvider>
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel size="sm">Project</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton isActive tooltip="Overview">
                <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Home /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
                <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Overview</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              </SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
    <SidebarFooter><SidebarTrigger /></SidebarFooter>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Collapsible Sections
Build collapsible nested menus with chevron toggles for documentation and API reference sidebars.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="none">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar variant="docs" style={{ width: "260px" }}>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarMenuItem expanded={isExpanded}>
          <SidebarMenuButton onClick={() => toggle(id)}>
            <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Getting Started</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
            <ChevronRightSm className="ml-auto transition-transform" />
          </SidebarMenuButton>
        </SidebarMenuItem>
        <SidebarMenuSub>
          <SidebarMenuSubItem>
            <SidebarMenuSubButton isActive>Introduction</SidebarMenuSubButton>
          </SidebarMenuSubItem>
          ...
        </SidebarMenuSub>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Search and Filter
Combine search and type-based filtering with nested tree navigation. Each item has an icon based on its type. A multi-select Select filters items by type.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="none">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 650 }}>
  <Sidebar style={{ width: "280px" }}>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <div className="flex items-center gap-1.5">
        <SidebarInput size="sm" placeholder="Search" ... />
        <Select
          multiple
          clearable
          placeholder="Filter"
          variant="outline"
          size="sm"
          options={stepFilterOptions}
          value={typeFilters}
          onChange={(selected) =>
            setTypeFilters(selected.map((o) => o.value))
          }
          block={false}
        />
      </div>
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton isActive>
                <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Desktop /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
                <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Start</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
              </SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Tree with Hover Actions
Tree navigation with chevrons on the left and action buttons on the right. Clicking a row selects the item. Chevrons toggle expand/collapse. Action buttons (... and +) appear on hover for parent items.
```tsx
<SidebarMenuItem className="group/action">
<SidebarMenuButton isActive onClick={() => setActiveItem(id)}>
  <SidebarMenuChevron className="!ml-0 ..."
    onClick={(e) => { e.stopPropagation(); toggleExpanded(id); }}
  />
  <SidebarMenuButtonIcon><Icon /></SidebarMenuButtonIcon>
  <SidebarMenuButtonLabel>Label</SidebarMenuButtonLabel>
  <span className="ml-auto opacity-0 group-hover/action:opacity-100">
    <Button variant="ghost" size="xs" uniform>
      <DotsHorizontal />
    </Button>
    <Button variant="ghost" size="xs" uniform>
      <Plus />
    </Button>
  </span>
</SidebarMenuButton>
<SidebarMenuSub open hasIcons>...</SidebarMenuSub>
</SidebarMenuItem>
```

### Mobile Menu
Mobile behavior is handled automatically when using SidebarProvider. The SidebarMobileMenuButton provides a standard animated hamburger trigger.
```tsx
// Desktop: standard sidebar with icon collapse
<SidebarProvider collapsible="icon">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar>...</Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>

// Mobile: phone-sized container with hamburger menu
<SidebarProvider collapsible="offcanvas">
<header>
  <SidebarMobileMenuButton />
</header>
{openMobile ? <SidebarContent>...</SidebarContent> : <div>Page content</div>}
</SidebarProvider>
```

### Search Input
The sidebar provides a dedicated SidebarInput component for search functionality.
```tsx
<SidebarProvider collapsible="none">
<SidebarLayout style={{ height: 500 }}>
  <Sidebar variant="docs" style={{ width: "220px" }}>
    <SidebarHeader>
      <SidebarInput
        placeholder="Search"
        value={searchValue}
        onChange={(e) => setSearchValue(e.target.value)}
        onClear={() => setSearchValue("")}
      />
    </SidebarHeader>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel>Get started</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuSubButton indent={0} isActive>Overview</SidebarMenuSubButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
            ...
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>...</SidebarInset>
</SidebarLayout>
</SidebarProvider>
```

## Skeleton
Loading placeholders that match the shape of the content they stand in for, from avatars and text to cards, forms, and tables.
Import: import { Skeleton } from "@plexui/ui/components/Skeleton"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/skeleton
Props:
  - circle (boolean) default: false — Render a circular skeleton
  - className (string) — Set dimensions and custom styling

### Overview
Use a circular skeleton to represent loading avatars, combined with text placeholders.
```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
<Skeleton circle className="size-12" />
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[200px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Card
Compose multiple skeletons to represent loading cards with images and text content.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 w-[300px] p-4 border border-default rounded-xl">
<Skeleton className="h-[150px] w-full rounded-lg" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-3/4" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-1/2" />
</div>
```

### Text
Multiple text lines with varying widths create natural-looking paragraph placeholders.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[300px]">
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-full" />
<Skeleton className="h-4 w-4/5" />
</div>
```

### Form
Form skeletons use Plex UI control sizing (32px height for inputs and buttons).
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4 w-[300px]">
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-10 w-full rounded-lg" />
</div>
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-10 w-full rounded-lg" />
</div>
<Skeleton className="h-10 w-[120px] rounded-lg" />
</div>
```

### Table
Table skeletons show header and row structure while data loads.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 w-[400px]">
<div className="flex gap-4 pb-2 border-b border-default">
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
  <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
</div>
{Array.from({ length: 4 }).map((_, i) => (
  <div key={i} className="flex gap-4 py-2">
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[100px]" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[150px]" />
    <Skeleton className="h-4 w-[80px]" />
  </div>
))}
</div>
```

## Slider
Slider for fine-tuning numeric values with single or range thumbs, marks, an editable value input, and vertical orientation.
Import: import { Slider } from "@plexui/ui/components/Slider"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/slider
Props:
  - value (number | number[]) — Current value; array when range is true
  - min (number) — Minimum value
  - max (number) — Maximum value
  - step (number) — Step increment
  - range (boolean) default: false — Enable multi-thumb range mode
  - orientation ("horizontal" | "vertical") default: "horizontal" — Layout direction of the slider
  - resetValue (number) — Value for reset option (single mode only)
  - resetTooltip (string) default: "Reset to default" — Tooltip and accessible name of the reset button
  - unit (string) — Unit displayed (e.g. ms, px)
  - prefixUnit (string) — Unit displayed before the value (e.g. $)
  - label (ReactNode) — Label (string or JSX). Also names the slider thumbs for assistive technology
  - marks (Array<{ value: number, label: string }>) — Marks below track (horizontal only)
  - onChange ((value: number | number[]) => void) — Change handler; receives array when range is true
  - minStepsBetweenThumbs (number) — Minimum steps between thumbs (range mode only)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Disable slider
  - trackColor (string) — Color of the slider track
  - rangeColor (string) — Color of the filled range
  - className (string) — Applied to the root element

### Overview
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState(1000)
<Slider
label="Example field"
min={0}
max={2000}
resetValue={1000}
step={10}
unit="ms"
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
/>
```

### Adding a tooltip
A tooltip can easily be added to the Slider label by providing JSX instead of a simple string.
```tsx
<Slider
label={
  <Tooltip content="More details about this field">
    <Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>Example field</Tooltip.TriggerDecorator>
  </Tooltip>
}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
...
/>
```

### Marks
Slider marks can be easily added by passing an array of values to the marks prop. Responsive behaviors are handled automatically.
```tsx
<Slider
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
label="Passing grade"
min={1}
max={5}
step={1}
marks={[
  { value: 1, label: "1" },
  { value: 2, label: "2" },
  ...
]}
trackColor="#61C454"
rangeColor="#EF4146"
/>
```

### Range
Set range to enable a dual-thumb slider for selecting a value range. The value and onChange props accept arrays instead of single numbers.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState([25, 75])
<Slider
range
label="Price range"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
prefixUnit="$"
/>
```

### Multiple thumbs
Pass three or more values to create a multi-thumb slider. Use minStepsBetweenThumbs to enforce minimum spacing between thumbs.
```tsx
const [value, setValue] = useState([10, 40, 70])
<Slider
range
label="Breakpoints"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
minStepsBetweenThumbs={5}
/>
```

### Vertical
Set orientation="vertical" to render a vertical slider. Marks are not supported in vertical orientation.
```tsx
<Slider
label="Volume"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={value}
onChange={setValue}
orientation="vertical"
/>
```

### Disabled
Set disabled to prevent interaction with the slider.
```tsx
<Slider
label="Disabled"
min={0}
max={100}
step={1}
value={50}
onChange={() => {}}
disabled
/>
```

## Stat Card
Stat card for dashboards displaying KPIs with trend deltas, an info tooltip, an icon, a progress bar, and accent border styling.
Import: import { StatCard } from "@plexui/ui/components/StatCard"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/stat-card
Props:
  - label (string) — Label describing the metric
  - value (ReactNode) — The primary metric value
  - description (string) — Subtitle below the value
  - trend ({ value: number; label?: string }) — Trend indicator with percentage
  - invertTrend (boolean) default: false — Invert trend colors (positive = bad)
  - trendPosition ("value" | "header") default: "value" — Where the trend indicator is rendered
  - trendVariant ("text" | "badge") default: "text" — Render trend as text or badge
  - size ("default" | "sm") default: "default" — Card size. Use sm for compact analytics layouts
  - icon (ReactNode) — Icon displayed on the left with a soft background
  - sparkline (ReactNode) — Chart rendered at the bottom
  - progress (number) — Progress bar value (0-100)
  - progressLabel (string) — Label next to progress bar
  - tooltip (string) — Shows an info icon next to the label with tooltip text
  - variant ("default" | "accent") default: "default" — Visual variant
  - accentColor ("primary" | "secondary" | "danger" | "info" | "discovery" | "success" | "caution" | "warning") default: "primary" — Left border color (accent variant)

### Overview
Dashboard-ready stat cards with trends, icons, and progress bars. Use the controls below to explore all available props.
```tsx
const [size, setSize] = useState("default")
const [variant, setVariant] = useState("default")
const [trendPosition, setTrendPosition] = useState("value")
const [trendVariant, setTrendVariant] = useState("text")
const [showTrend, setShowTrend] = useState(true)
const [showTooltip, setShowTooltip] = useState(false)
const [invertTrend, setInvertTrend] = useState(false)

<StatCard
label="Total Revenue"
value="$45,231"
size={size}
variant={variant}
trendPosition={trendPosition}
trendVariant={trendVariant}
trend={showTrend ? { value: 12.5, label: "vs last month" } : undefined}
tooltip={showTooltip ? "Sum of all revenue streams" : undefined}
invertTrend={invertTrend}
/>
```

### Sizes
Use size="sm" for compact analytics rows with denser spacing and smaller typography. The small size also pairs well with the tooltip prop for info icons.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-6">
{/* Default size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-4">
  <StatCard label="Total Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
  <StatCard label="Active Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
  <StatCard label="Conversion Rate" value="3.24%" trend={{ value: -1.8 }} />
</div>
{/* Small size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3">
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Total Inquiries" value="3,544" trend={{ value: -2.6 }} tooltip="Total inquiries in period" />
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Completion Rate" value="89.2%" trend={{ value: 0.5 }} tooltip="Average across templates" />
  <StatCard size="sm" label="Approval Rate" value="84.6%" trend={{ value: 1.8 }} tooltip="Average across templates" />
</div>
</div>
```

### Trend position
Control where the trend appears: next to the value (default) or right-aligned in the header row.
```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
<StatCard label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} trendPosition="value" />
<StatCard label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} trendPosition="header" />
</div>
```

### Trend variant
Display the trend as plain text or wrapped in a badge.
```tsx
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4" style={{ maxWidth: 480 }}>
<StatCard label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} trendVariant="text" />
<StatCard label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} trendVariant="badge" />
</div>
```

### Info tooltip
Pass a tooltip string to render an info icon next to the label with a tooltip on hover.
```tsx
<StatCard label="Avg Completion Rate" value="89.2%" trend={{ value: 0.5 }} tooltip="Percentage of inquiries reaching final state" />
```

### With icon
Pass an icon to display it on the left side with a soft background. The layout automatically switches to a horizontal icon + content arrangement. Works with both default and sm sizes.
```tsx
import { DollarCircle, Users, ShoppingBag } from "@plexui/ui/components/Icon"

{/* Default size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
<StatCard icon={<DollarCircle />} label="Total Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
<StatCard icon={<Users />} label="Active Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
</div>

{/* Small size */}
<div className="grid grid-cols-3 gap-3">
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<DollarCircle />} label="Revenue" value="$45,231" trend={{ value: 12.5 }} />
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<Users />} label="Users" value="2,847" trend={{ value: 8.2 }} />
<StatCard size="sm" icon={<ShoppingBag />} label="Orders" value="1,234" trend={{ value: -3.1 }} />
</div>
```

### With progress
Progress bars show a visual representation of completion or usage percentage.
```tsx
<StatCard label="Storage Used" value="7.2 GB" progress={72} progressLabel="72%" description="of 10 GB" />
```

### Accent border
The accent variant adds a colored left border. Choose from six semantic colors.
```tsx
const [accentColor, setAccentColor] = useState("primary")

<StatCard
label="Total Revenue"
value="$45,231"
variant="accent"
accentColor={accentColor}
trend={{ value: 12.5, label: "vs last month" }}
/>
```

### Inverted trend
Use invertTrend for metrics where positive values are bad (e.g., error rate, response time). Toggle the switch to see the color flip.
```tsx
const [invertTrend, setInvertTrend] = useState(true)

<StatCard
label="Avg Response Time"
value="234ms"
trend={{ value: 15.3, label: "vs last hour" }}
invertTrend={invertTrend}
/>
```

## Switch
Toggle switch for turning settings on or off, with an optional label, a supporting description linked for screen readers, and a configurable label position.
Import: import { Switch } from "@plexui/ui/components/Switch"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/switch
Props:
  - checked (boolean) — Controlled state
  - defaultChecked (boolean) — Initial state (uncontrolled)
  - onCheckedChange ((next: boolean) => void) — Called when toggled
  - label (ReactNode) — Accessible label rendered next to the switch
  - description (ReactNode) — Secondary text below the label, linked via aria-describedby
  - labelPosition ("start" | "end") default: "end" — Label on left (start) or right (end)
  - disabled (boolean) default: false — Prevent interaction
  - required (boolean) — Required for form submission
  - name (string) — Form field name
  - value (string) — Value when submitted
  - className (string) — CSS classes applied to wrapper node
  - id (string) — The id of the switch element

### Overview
```tsx
<Switch aria-label="Notifications" />
```

### With label
Add a label using the label prop. The label is automatically connected to the switch via id.
```tsx
<Switch label="Notifications" />
```

### With description
Add a description below the label for additional context. Linked to the switch via aria-describedby.
```tsx
<Switch
label="Disable user API keys"
description="Disable user-based API keys across your entire organization."
/>
```

### Label position
Set {'labelPosition="start"'} to place the label on the left side of the switch control.
```tsx
<Switch label="Right aligned" labelPosition="start" />
```

### Label position with description
The description follows the label position: both move together when {'labelPosition="start"'} is set.
```tsx
<Switch
label="Dark mode"
description="Use dark theme across the entire application."
labelPosition="start"
/>
```

### Default checked
Initialize the switch with defaultChecked when you don't need to control its state. Use the name prop to read the value on form submission.
```tsx
<Switch label="Enable notifications" name="notifications" defaultChecked />
```

### Controlled
Pass checked and onCheckedChange to manage the state in a controlled manner.
```tsx
const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false)
<Switch label="Airplane mode" checked={checked} onCheckedChange={setChecked} />
```

### Disabled
Use disabled to prevent the user from toggling the control.
```tsx
<div className="flex gap-6">
<Switch disabled aria-label="Notifications" />
<Switch disabled checked aria-label="Dark mode" />
</div>
```

### Disabled with label
Disabled state works with labels: both the toggle and the label show a not-allowed cursor.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Switch label="Notifications" disabled />
<Switch label="Notifications" disabled defaultChecked />
</div>
```

### Disabled with description
Combine disabled with label and description for read-only settings that need explanation.
```tsx
<div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
<Switch
  label="Enable SSO"
  description="Requires an Enterprise plan to configure."
  disabled
/>
<Switch
  label="Two-factor authentication"
  description="Enforced by organization policy."
  disabled
  defaultChecked
/>
</div>
```

### With Field
Pair a Switch with Field using orientation="horizontal" for inline toggle settings.
```tsx
<Field label="Marketing emails" orientation="horizontal">
{(fieldProps) => (
  <Switch id={fieldProps.id} checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} />
)}
</Field>
```

### With Field and description
Use Field with description for the settings pattern with a section heading, description, and a labeled switch underneath.
```tsx
<Field
label="Access Control"
description="Disable user-based API keys across your entire organization. You can also choose to disable them on a project-by-project basis if needed."
>
{(fieldProps) => (
  <Switch
    id={fieldProps.id}
    label="Disable user API keys"
    checked={enabled}
    onCheckedChange={setEnabled}
  />
)}
</Field>
```

### Settings panel
Combine label and description to build settings-style toggle panels.
```tsx
<div className="flex w-full max-w-lg flex-col gap-8">
<Switch
  label="Enable custom providers for evals"
  description="Allow eval runs to use third-party models you configure under Custom model providers."
/>
<Switch
  label="Enable OpenRouter models"
  description="Make OpenRouter models available for evaluation runs."
/>
<Switch
  label="Disable user API keys"
  description="Disable user-based API keys across your entire organization."
  defaultChecked
/>
</div>
```

### Grouped sections
Use dividers to separate switch groups into logical sections. Each section can be wrapped in a Field with its own label and description.
```tsx
<div className="w-full max-w-lg divide-y divide-alpha/15">
<div className="pb-5">
  <Field label="Notifications" description="Configure how you receive notifications.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        <Switch
          label="Push notifications"
          description="Receive push notifications on your devices."
          defaultChecked
        />
        <Switch
          label="Email notifications"
          description="Get notified via email for important updates."
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
<div className="pt-5">
  <Field label="Privacy" description="Control your data sharing preferences.">
    {() => (
      <div className="flex flex-col gap-4">
        <Switch
          label="Share usage data"
          description="Help us improve by sharing anonymous usage statistics."
        />
        <Switch
          label="Personalized content"
          description="Allow personalized recommendations based on your activity."
          defaultChecked
        />
      </div>
    )}
  </Field>
</div>
</div>
```

## Table
Styled table primitives for structured data, with header, body, footer, row, cell and caption parts on native table elements.
Import: import { Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableRow, TableHead, TableCell } from "@plexui/ui/components/Table"
Import: import { DataTable, DataTableColumnHeader } from "@plexui/ui/components/DataTable"
Docs: https://plexui.com/components/table
  Table Primitives:
    - Table (table) — Root table container with horizontal scroll wrapper
    - TableHeader (thead) — Table header group
    - TableBody (tbody) — Table body group
    - TableFooter (tfoot) — Table footer group
    - TableRow (tr) — Table row
    - TableHead (th) — Table header cell
    - TableCell (td) — Table data cell
    - TableCaption (caption) — Table caption
  DataTable:
    - columns (ColumnDef<TData>[]) — Column definitions following TanStack Table v8 API
    - data (TData[]) — Data array to display
    - variant ("default" | "bordered") default: "default" — Visual variant: bordered adds a rounded border and tinted header
    - pageSize (number) default: 10 — Rows per page. Set 0 or Infinity to disable pagination
    - initialSorting (SortingState) — Initial column sorting state
    - globalFilter (string) — Controlled search/filter string
    - onGlobalFilterChange ((value: string) => void) — Callback when filter changes
    - onRowClick ((row: TData) => void) — Click handler for rows, makes rows interactive
    - columnVisibility (VisibilityState) — Controlled column visibility state
    - onColumnVisibilityChange ((visibility: VisibilityState) => void) — Callback when visibility changes
    - enableRowSelection (boolean) default: false — Enable row selection checkboxes
    - rowSelection (RowSelectionState) — Controlled row selection state
    - onRowSelectionChange ((selection: RowSelectionState) => void) — Callback when selection changes
    - getRowId ((row: TData) => string) — Custom row ID accessor
    - emptyMessage (ReactNode) default: "No results." — Shown when no rows
    - showPagination (boolean) default: true — Whether to show pagination controls
    - className (string) — Class applied to outermost wrapper
  DataTableColumnHeader:
    - column (Column<TData, TValue>) — TanStack Table column object
    - title (string) — Display text for the header
  Column helpers:
    - idCell(accessor) (CellComponent) — Monospace ID with copy-on-click tooltip
    - dateTimeCell(accessor, options?) (CellComponent) — Formatted datetime with Intl.DateTimeFormat
    - statusCell(accessor, colorMap?) (CellComponent) — Badge cell with automatic status-to-color mapping
    - tooltipHeader(label, description) (HeaderComponent) — Header with dashed underline and info tooltip

### Overview
A complete table with header, body, footer, and caption showing invoice data.
```tsx
const invoices = [
{ invoice: "INV001", status: "Paid", method: "Credit Card", amount: "$250.00" },
{ invoice: "INV002", status: "Pending", method: "PayPal", amount: "$150.00" },
{ invoice: "INV003", status: "Unpaid", method: "Bank Transfer", amount: "$350.00" },
{ invoice: "INV004", status: "Paid", method: "Credit Card", amount: "$450.00" },
{ invoice: "INV005", status: "Paid", method: "PayPal", amount: "$550.00" },
]

<Table>
<TableCaption>A list of your recent invoices.</TableCaption>
<TableHeader>
  <TableRow>
    <TableHead>Invoice</TableHead>
    <TableHead>Status</TableHead>
    <TableHead>Method</TableHead>
    <TableHead className="text-right">Amount</TableHead>
  </TableRow>
</TableHeader>
<TableBody>
  {invoices.map((invoice) => (
    <TableRow key={invoice.invoice}>
      <TableCell className="font-medium">{invoice.invoice}</TableCell>
      <TableCell>{invoice.status}</TableCell>
      <TableCell>{invoice.method}</TableCell>
      <TableCell className="text-right">{invoice.amount}</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  ))}
</TableBody>
<TableFooter>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell colSpan={3}>Total</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$1,750.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</TableFooter>
</Table>
```

### With footer
A table with a footer row displaying subtotal information.
```tsx
<Table>
<TableHeader>
  <TableRow>
    <TableHead>Product</TableHead>
    <TableHead className="text-right">Qty</TableHead>
    <TableHead className="text-right">Price</TableHead>
    <TableHead className="text-right">Total</TableHead>
  </TableRow>
</TableHeader>
<TableBody>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell className="font-medium">Pro Plan</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">3</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$29.00</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$87.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell className="font-medium">Storage Add-on</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">1</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$9.00</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right">$9.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</TableBody>
<TableFooter>
  <TableRow>
    <TableCell colSpan={3}>Subtotal</TableCell>
    <TableCell className="text-right font-semibold">$96.00</TableCell>
  </TableRow>
</TableFooter>
</Table>
```

### Minimal
A simple table without caption or footer, showing a list of people.
```tsx
const people = [
{ name: "Lindsay Walton", title: "Front-end Developer", email: "lindsay@example.com" },
{ name: "Courtney Henry", title: "Designer", email: "courtney@example.com" },
{ name: "Tom Cook", title: "Director of Product", email: "tom@example.com" },
]

<Table>
<TableHeader>
  <TableRow>
    <TableHead>Name</TableHead>
    <TableHead>Title</TableHead>
    <TableHead>Email</TableHead>
  </TableRow>
</TableHeader>
<TableBody>
  {people.map((person) => (
    <TableRow key={person.email}>
      <TableCell className="font-medium">{person.name}</TableCell>
      <TableCell>{person.title}</TableCell>
```
